display.text:
"""Tests for first-run onboarding signal extraction and gating."""

from __future__ import annotations

from types import SimpleNamespace

import pytest
from agentic_odi_cli import onboard, profile


class _Response:
    def __init__(self, text: str, url: str = "https://acme.test/product") -> None:
        self.text = text
        self.url = url

    def raise_for_status(self) -> None:
        return None


def test_page_signals_repr_summarises_the_fetch() -> None:
    signals = onboard.PageSignals(
        title="Acme",
        meta_description="desc",
        domain="acme.test",
        primary_user=None,
        business_model=None,
        core_problem=None,
        current_focus=None,
        confidence="high",
    )

    assert signals.title == "Acme"
    assert "Acme" in repr(signals)
    assert "acme.test" in repr(signals)


def test_infer_baseline_marks_keyword_rich_pages_high_confidence() -> None:
    signals = onboard.PageSignals(
        title="DevTools error tracking and monitoring",
        meta_description="performance analytics",
        domain="acme.test",
        primary_user="engineers",
        business_model="saas",
        core_problem="debugging",
        current_focus="launch",
        confidence=None,
    )

    baseline, scores = onboard.infer_baseline(signals)

    assert baseline.source == "url"
    assert baseline.domain == "acme.test"
    assert baseline.primary_user == "engineers"
    assert baseline.confidence == "high"
    assert scores["devtools"] == 3
    assert scores["error"] == 2


def test_infer_baseline_marks_keyword_poor_pages_low_confidence() -> None:
    signals = onboard.PageSignals(
        title="Acme",
        meta_description="A friendly product",
        domain=None,
        primary_user=None,
        business_model=None,
        core_problem=None,
        current_focus=None,
        confidence=None,
    )

    baseline, scores = onboard.infer_baseline(signals)

    assert baseline.domain == ""
    assert baseline.confidence == "low"
    assert scores == {}


def test_extract_signals_reads_title_meta_and_domain() -> None:
    html = (
        "<html><head><title>Acme DevTools</title>"
        '<meta name="description" content="Error tracking for teams">'
        "</head></html>"
    )

    signals = onboard._extract_signals(html, "https://acme.test/product")

    assert signals.title == "Acme DevTools"
    assert signals.meta_description == "Error tracking for teams"
    assert signals.domain == "acme.test"
    assert signals.confidence == "high"


def test_extract_signals_defaults_missing_metadata_to_empty() -> None:
    signals = onboard._extract_signals("<html></html>", "https://acme.test")

    assert signals.title == ""
    assert signals.meta_description == ""
    assert signals.confidence == "low"


def test_fetch_signals_returns_a_baseline_for_reachable_pages(monkeypatch) -> None:
    html = "<html><head><title>DevTools error tracking</title></head></html>"
    monkeypatch.setattr(onboard.httpx, "get", lambda *args, **kwargs: _Response(html))

    baseline, low_confidence = onboard.fetch_signals("https://acme.test")

    assert baseline.domain == "acme.test"
    assert baseline.confidence == "high"
    assert low_confidence is False


def test_fetch_signals_falls_back_to_typed_path_on_fetch_errors(monkeypatch) -> None:
    def _boom(*args, **kwargs):
        raise RuntimeError("offline")

    monkeypatch.setattr(onboard.httpx, "get", _boom)

    signals, low_confidence = onboard.fetch_signals("https://acme.test")

    assert isinstance(signals, onboard.PageSignals)
    assert signals.title == ""
    assert signals.confidence == "low"
    assert low_confidence is True


def test_fetch_signals_falls_back_when_the_status_is_an_error(monkeypatch) -> None:
    class _ErrorResponse(_Response):
        def raise_for_status(self) -> None:
            raise RuntimeError("500")

    monkeypatch.setattr(onboard.httpx, "get", lambda *args, **kwargs: _ErrorResponse("ignored"))

    signals, low_confidence = onboard.fetch_signals("https://acme.test")

    assert isinstance(signals, onboard.PageSignals)
    assert signals.title == ""
    assert low_confidence is True


def test_contract_copy_is_available() -> None:
    assert any("consent" in line for line in onboard.HONESTY_CONTRACT_LINES)
    assert any("Product" in line for line in onboard.CARD_LINES)


def _interactive(monkeypatch) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setattr(onboard.sys, "stdin", SimpleNamespace(isatty=lambda: True))
    monkeypatch.setattr(onboard.sys, "stdout", SimpleNamespace(isatty=lambda: True))


def test_maybe_run_first_launch_skips_when_no_onboard(monkeypatch, capsys) -> None:
    _interactive(monkeypatch)

    onboard.maybe_run_first_launch(no_onboard=True)

    assert capsys.readouterr().out == ""


def test_maybe_run_first_launch_skips_when_a_baseline_exists(monkeypatch, capsys) -> None:
    _interactive(monkeypatch)
    monkeypatch.setattr(profile, "baseline_exists", lambda: True)

    onboard.maybe_run_first_launch()

    assert capsys.readouterr().out == ""


def test_maybe_run_first_launch_skips_without_a_tty(monkeypatch, capsys) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setattr(onboard.sys, "stdin", SimpleNamespace(isatty=lambda: False))
    monkeypatch.setattr(onboard.sys, "stdout", SimpleNamespace(isatty=lambda: True))
    monkeypatch.setattr(profile, "baseline_exists", lambda: False)

    onboard.maybe_run_first_launch()

    assert capsys.readouterr().out == ""


@pytest.mark.parametrize("subcommand", ["setup", "profile", "version", "help"])
def test_maybe_run_first_launch_skips_management_subcommands(
    monkeypatch, capsys, subcommand
) -> None:
    _interactive(monkeypatch)
    monkeypatch.setattr(profile, "baseline_exists", lambda: False)

    onboard.maybe_run_first_launch(invoked_subcommand=subcommand)

    assert capsys.readouterr().out == ""


def test_maybe_run_first_launch_shows_the_card(monkeypatch) -> None:
    _interactive(monkeypatch)
    monkeypatch.setattr(profile, "baseline_exists", lambda: False)
    printed: list[str] = []
    monkeypatch.setattr(onboard.typer, "echo", printed.append)

    onboard.maybe_run_first_launch()

    output = "".join(printed)
    assert "First-run onboarding card" in output
    assert "consent" in output

"""Edge-case tests for the connectors CLI adapter."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json

from agentic_odi_cli import connectors
from agentic_odi_cli.cli import app
from agentic_odi_connectors.models import HealthStatus
from typer.testing import CliRunner

runner = CliRunner()


def test_lazy_wrappers_call_the_connectors_package() -> None:
    from agentic_odi_connectors.models import ConnectorConfig

    built = connectors.build_connector(
        ConnectorConfig(name="gong", kind="mcp", settings={"url": "http://localhost:9000/mcp"})
    )
    sink = connectors.get_default_sink()

    assert built.__class__.__name__ == "MCPClientConnector"
    assert sink.__class__.__name__ == "IngestSink"


def test_config_path_prefers_the_environment(monkeypatch, tmp_path) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setenv("AGENTIC_ODI_CONNECTORS_CONFIG", str(tmp_path / "env.json"))

    assert connectors._config_path(None) == tmp_path / "env.json"
    assert connectors._config_path(tmp_path / "explicit.json") == tmp_path / "explicit.json"


def test_config_path_matches_the_connectors_package(monkeypatch, tmp_path) -> None:
    from agentic_odi_connectors.paths import config_path

    monkeypatch.delenv("AGENTIC_ODI_CONNECTORS_CONFIG", raising=False)
    monkeypatch.setenv("HOME", str(tmp_path / "home"))

    assert connectors._config_path(None) == config_path()
    assert config_path() == tmp_path / "home" / ".config" / "agentic-odi" / "connectors.json"


def test_config_path_defaults_to_the_config_directory(monkeypatch, tmp_path) -> None:
    monkeypatch.delenv("AGENTIC_ODI_CONNECTORS_CONFIG", raising=False)
    monkeypatch.setenv("HOME", str(tmp_path / "home"))

    expected = tmp_path / "home" / ".config" / "agentic-odi" / "connectors.json"
    assert connectors._config_path(None) == expected

display.text:
"""Edge tests for the root CLI callback and update re-exec."""

from __future__ import annotations

from types import SimpleNamespace
from typing import Any

import agentic_odi_cli.cli as cli_module
from agentic_odi_cli.cli import app
from typer.testing import CliRunner


def test_no_args_launches_chat_when_attached_to_a_terminal(monkeypatch) -> None:
    seen: list = []
    monkeypatch.setattr(cli_module.sys, "stdin", SimpleNamespace(isatty=lambda: True))
    monkeypatch.setattr(cli_module.sys, "stdout", SimpleNamespace(isatty=lambda: True))
    monkeypatch.setattr("agentic_odi_cli.chat.run_chat", lambda config: seen.append(config))

    ctx: Any = SimpleNamespace(invoked_subcommand=None)
    cli_module.main(
        ctx,
        version=False,
        verbose=False,
        backend=None,
        db=None,
        mcp_url=None,
        no_update=True,
    )

    assert len(seen) == 1


def test_chat_command_uses_explicit_connection_options(monkeypatch) -> None:
    seen: list = []
    monkeypatch.setattr("agentic_odi_cli.chat.run_chat", lambda config: seen.append(config))

    result = CliRunner().invoke(
        app,
        [
            "--no-update",
            "chat",
            "--base-url",
            "http://llm/v1",
            "--api-key",
            "secret",
            "--model",
            "custom",
            "--mcp-url",
            "http://mcp",
        ],
    )

    assert result.exit_code == 0
    config = seen[0]
    assert config.base_url == "http://llm/v1"
    assert config.api_key == "secret"
    assert config.model == "custom"
    assert config.mcp_url == "http://mcp"


def test_reexec_current_replaces_the_process(monkeypatch, tmp_path) -> None:
    version_dir = tmp_path / "versions" / "0.2.0"
    version_dir.mkdir(parents=True)
    binary = version_dir / "odi"
    binary.write_text("#!/bin/sh\n")
    current = tmp_path / "current"
    current.symlink_to(version_dir, target_is_directory=True)
    monkeypatch.setattr(cli_module.paths, "current_link", lambda: current)
    monkeypatch.setattr(cli_module.sys, "argv", ["odi", "update", "--now"])
    calls: list[tuple] = []
    monkeypatch.setattr(cli_module.os, "execv", lambda path, argv: calls.append((path, argv)))

    cli_module._reexec_current()

    assert calls == [(str(current / "odi"), [str(current / "odi")])]


def test_reexec_current_defers_when_not_installed(monkeypatch, tmp_path, capsys) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setattr(cli_module.paths, "current_link", lambda: tmp_path / "missing")

    cli_module._reexec_current()

    assert "take effect on the next run" in capsys.readouterr().out

@capabilities_app.callback(invoke_without_command=True)
def capabilities_cmd(
    json_output: bool = typer.Option(
        False, "--json", help="Emit machine-readable JSON manifest."
    ),
) -> None:
    """Print what the assistant can do."""
    from agentic_odi_core import capability_manifest, capability_summary

    if json_output:
        typer.echo(json.dumps(capability_manifest(), indent=2))
    else:
        typer.echo(capability_summary())


@capabilities_app.command(name="tools")
def capabilities_tools() -> None:
    """List tool names only."""
    from agentic_odi_core import TOOL_NAMES

    for name in TOOL_NAMES:

1: # CLI Reference
2: 
3: The `agentic-odi` CLI is a [`Typer`](https://github.com/fastapi/typer)-based
4: command-line interface for working with Agentic ODI without a chat UI. It
5: provides an interactive chat mode plus version, update, and data commands. Data
6: commands are **local-first**: they read and write a SQLite store with no server
7: required, and switch to a remote MCP server with `--backend mcp`.
8: 
9: Install the workspace first if you have not already:
10: 
11: ```bash
12: uv sync --all-packages
13: ```
14: 
15: ## Launching
16: 
17: ```bash
18: python -m agentic_odi_cli --version   # print the Agentic ODI version
19: python -m agentic_odi_cli --help      # show available options and commands
20: python -m agentic_odi_cli             # start interactive chat in a terminal (help when piped)
21: ```
22: 
23: A console script is also installed, so `agentic-odi --version` works the same way.
24: 
25: ## Global options
26: 
27: | Option | Environment variable | Default | Meaning |
28: |---|---|---|---|
29: | `--backend local\|mcp` | `AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND` | `local` | Run in-process against SQLite, or call a remote MCP server. |
30: | `--db PATH` | `AGENTIC_ODI_DB` | `~/.agentic-odi/odi.db` | Store path for the `local` backend. |
31: | `--mcp-url URL` | `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` | `http://localhost:8000/mcp` | Server URL for the `mcp` backend. |
32: 
33: Data commands print readable tables and blocks by default; add `--json` for
34: machine-readable output. Diagnostics go to stderr and failures exit non-zero
35: (`0` success, `1` error, `2` usage error).
36: 
37: ## Interactive chat
38: 
39: `agentic-odi chat` (or simply `agentic-odi` in a terminal) starts an
40: offline-first interactive REPL. The session always boots, even when no model or
41: MCP server is reachable — a yellow warning is shown for any unavailable service,
42: and free-text messages return a friendly nudge until you connect.
43: 
44: ```bash
45: agentic-odi chat
46: agentic-odi chat --model local-tools-model --mcp-url http://localhost:8000/mcp
47: ```
48: 
49: ### Connection settings
50: 
51: The chat resolves settings in priority order:
52: **CLI flag → environment variable → persisted profile → built-in default.**
53: 
54: | Variable | Default | CLI flag |
55: |---|---|---|
56: | `AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:8001/v1` | `--base-url` |
57: | `AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL` | `local-tools-model` | `--model` |
58: | `AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY` | `local` | `--api-key` |
59: | `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` | `http://localhost:8000/mcp` | `--mcp-url` |
60: 
61: The **persisted profile** is stored at
62: `~/.config/agentic-odi/llm_profile.json`. You can create or update it from
63: within the session using `/connect`.
64: 
65: ### Slash commands
66: 
67: | Command | Description |
68: |---|---|
69: | `/help` | Show all available commands |
70: | `/status` | Show current model, base URL, and MCP server with connection status |
71: | `/connect` | Launch the wizard: provider → URL → API key → model → MCP URL → save |
72: | `/model <name>` | Hot-swap to a different model mid-session |
73: | `/mcp <url>` | Reconnect to a different MCP server mid-session |
74: | `/tools` | List the MCP tools the assistant can call |
75: | `/clear` | Reset conversation history (keeps connection) |
76: | `/exit` | Quit the session (also `/quit`) |
77: 
78: ### /connect wizard
79: 
80: `/connect` walks you through configuring your LLM provider interactively:
81: 
82: 1. **Provider** — choose `openai`, `anthropic`, `local`, or `other`
83: 2. **Base URL** — preset filled for known providers; override freely
84: 3. **API key** — input is hidden via `getpass`
85: 4. **Model** — sensible default per provider
86: 5. **MCP URL** — defaults to the current value
87: 6. **Save to profile?** — writes `~/.config/agentic-odi/llm_profile.json` so settings persist across sessions
88: 
89: The wizard can be cancelled at any step with Ctrl-C.
90: 
91: > [!NOTE]
92: > Chat is the only CLI mode that needs an LLM endpoint. The `customer-outcomes`
93: > and `connectors` commands keep working without one.
94: 
95: ## Manage Jobs, Steps, and desired Outcomes
96: 
97: Every ODI entity has the same create/read/update/delete surface in the CLI and
98: the MCP server. Jobs hold Steps (the Job Map) and desired Outcomes; deleting a
99: Job cascades to both.
100: 
101: ```bash
102: # Jobs
103: agentic-odi jobs add --name "Onboard a customer" --description "First 30 days"
104: agentic-odi jobs list
105: agentic-odi jobs get <job-id>
106: agentic-odi jobs update <job-id> --name "Onboard a new customer"
107: agentic-odi jobs delete <job-id> --yes
108: 
109: # Steps (Job Map)
110: agentic-odi steps add --job-id <job-id> --name "Prepare environment" --order 1
111: agentic-odi steps list --job-id <job-id>
112: agentic-odi steps get <step-id>
113: agentic-odi steps update <step-id> --order 2
114: agentic-odi steps delete <step-id> --yes
115: 
116: # Desired Outcomes
117: agentic-odi desired-outcomes add --job-id <job-id>   --statement "Minimize the time it takes to get a working environment"   --importance 8 --satisfaction 4
118: agentic-odi desired-outcomes list --job-id <job-id>
119: agentic-odi desired-outcomes get <outcome-id>
120: agentic-odi desired-outcomes update <outcome-id> --satisfaction 6
121: agentic-odi desired-outcomes delete <outcome-id> --yes
122: ```
123: 
124: Add `--json` to any command for machine-readable output.
125: 
126: ## Evidence
127: 
128: Evidence is research captured from connectors (or entered by hand) and linked to
129: a Job, Step, or desired Outcome. Records can later be promoted into ODI
130: artifacts — the bridge from research to the model, without hand-copying.
131: 
132: ```bash
133: # Capture a record by hand
134: agentic-odi evidence add \
135:   --source-name "interview" --source-kind manual \
136:   --name "Support lead" \
137:   --content "Setup takes two days for every new engineer" \
138:   --job-id <job-id>
139: 
140: # Read and delete
141: agentic-odi evidence list --job-id <job-id>
142: agentic-odi evidence list --job-id <job-id> --json
143: agentic-odi evidence get <evidence-id>
144: agentic-odi evidence delete <evidence-id> --yes
145: 
146: # Promote into the ODI model
147: agentic-odi evidence promote <evidence-id> --to job
148: agentic-odi evidence promote <evidence-id> --to outcome --job-id <job-id>
149: ```
150: 
151: `connectors ingest --job-id <job-id>` maps every evidence-bearing record in the
152: ingested batch into evidence in one step.
153: 
154: ## Schema, scoring, and guidance
155: 
156: ```bash
157: agentic-odi schema            # canonical JSON schema for every ODI entity
158: agentic-odi score 8 2         # ODI opportunity score → 14.00
159: agentic-odi evaluate "Minimize the time to ship when onboarding"  # outcome-format check
160: agentic-odi evaluate --json "Minimize the time to ship when onboarding"
161: agentic-odi guidelines        # the ODI stage-by-stage guide
162: agentic-odi capabilities      # what the assistant can do
163: ```
164: 
165: `evaluate` returns the same verdict the `evaluate_outcome` MCP tool does, so the
166: check works with or without a running server.
167: 
168: ## Manage Customer Outcomes
169: 
170: Customer Outcomes link customer value to business value. The `local` backend
171: writes to the shared SQLite store with no server required; add `--backend mcp`
172: to route through a running MCP server (`python -m agentic_odi_mcp_server`). The group is also
173: available under its historical name `outcomes`.
174: 
175: ```bash
176: # Add a Customer Outcome
177: agentic-odi customer-outcomes add --job-id <job-id> \
178:   --direction minimize --unit "time" --object "to resolve setup errors" \
179:   --statement "Minimize the time to resolve environment setup errors when onboarding" \
180:   --importance 8.8 --satisfaction 3.2 \
181:   --category cost_reduction \
182:   --business-statement "Saves engineering hours and reduces early churn"
183: 
184: # Attach value metrics: repeatable JSON objects
185: agentic-odi customer-outcomes add --job-id <job-id> \
186:   --direction minimize --unit "time" --object "to resolve setup errors" \
187:   --statement "Minimize the time to resolve environment setup errors when onboarding" \
188:   --importance 8.8 --satisfaction 3.2 --category cost_reduction \
189:   --business-statement "Saves engineering hours" \
190:   --value-metric '{"name":"first response","direction":"minimize","unit_of_measure":"minutes","importance":7,"satisfaction":3}'
191: 
192: # List outcomes (optionally filtered, or as JSON)
193: agentic-odi customer-outcomes list
194: agentic-odi customer-outcomes list --job-id <job-id>
195: agentic-odi customer-outcomes list --json
196: 
197: # Get, update, delete
198: agentic-odi customer-outcomes get <outcome-id>
199: agentic-odi customer-outcomes update <outcome-id> --importance 9.0
200: agentic-odi customer-outcomes delete <outcome-id> --yes
201: 
202: # Compute an ODI Opportunity Score (top-level, also under the group)
203: agentic-odi score 8 2
204: agentic-odi outcomes score 8 2
205: ```
206: 
207: `score` applies the ODI opportunity formula,
208: `importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0)`.
209: 
210: Set `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` (or `--mcp-url`) to point to a non-default server when
211: using `--backend mcp` (default: `http://localhost:8000/mcp`).
212: 
213: ## Connectors
214: 
215: The `connectors` group manages external MCP integrations. See
216: [External Connectors](connectors.md) for presets, the connector registry, and
217: ingest behavior.
218: 
219: ```bash
220: python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors catalog
221: python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors add mcp --preset github
222: python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors list
223: python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors health --name github
224: python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors ingest --name github
225: ```
226: 
227: ## Updates
228: 
229: `odi update` checks for and installs a new binary release. Auto-update is on by
230: default; disable it with `--no-update` for one run or
231: `AGENTIC_ODI_NO_UPDATE=1` globally. See [Installation](installation.md).

(End of file - total 231 lines)
</content>

python -m agentic_odi_cli --version   # print the Agentic ODI version

display.text:
# CLI Reference

The `agentic-odi` CLI is a [`Typer`](https://github.com/fastapi/typer)-based
command-line interface for working with Agentic ODI without a chat UI. It
provides an interactive chat mode plus version, update, and data commands. Data
commands are **local-first**: they read and write a SQLite store with no server
required, and switch to a remote MCP server with `--backend mcp`.

Install the workspace first if you have not already:

```bash
uv sync --all-packages
```

## Launching

```bash
python -m agentic_odi_cli --version   # print the Agentic ODI version
python -m agentic_odi_cli --help      # show available options and commands
python -m agentic_odi_cli             # start interactive chat in a terminal (help when piped)
```

A console script is also installed, so `agentic-odi --version` works the same way.

## Global options

| Option | Environment variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--backend local\|mcp` | `AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND` | `local` | Run in-process against SQLite, or call a remote MCP server. |
| `--db PATH` | `AGENTIC_ODI_DB` | `~/.agentic-odi/odi.db` | Store path for the `local` backend. |
| `--mcp-url URL` | `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` | `http://localhost:8000/mcp` | Server URL for the `mcp` backend. |

Data commands print readable tables and blocks by default; add `--json` for
machine-readable output. Diagnostics go to stderr and failures exit non-zero
(`0` success, `1` error, `2` usage error).

## Interactive chat

`agentic-odi chat` (or simply `agentic-odi` in a terminal) starts an
offline-first interactive REPL. The session always boots, even when no model or
MCP server is reachable — a yellow warning is shown for any unavailable service,
and free-text messages return a friendly nudge until you connect.

```bash
agentic-odi chat
agentic-odi chat --model local-tools-model --mcp-url http://localhost:8000/mcp
```

### Connection settings

The chat resolves settings in priority order:
**CLI flag → environment variable → persisted profile → built-in default.**

| Variable | Default | CLI flag |
|---|---|---|
| `AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:8001/v1` | `--base-url` |
| `AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL` | `local-tools-model` | `--model` |
| `AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY` | `local` | `--api-key` |
| `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` | `http://localhost:8000/mcp` | `--mcp-url` |

The **persisted profile** is stored at
`~/.config/agentic-odi/llm_profile.json`. You can create or update it from
within the session using `/connect`.

### Slash commands

| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| `/help` | Show all available commands |
| `/status` | Show current model, base URL, and MCP server with connection status |
| `/connect` | Launch the wizard: provider → URL → API key → model → MCP URL → save |
| `/model <name>` | Hot-swap to a different model mid-session |
| `/mcp <url>` | Reconnect to a different MCP server mid-session |
| `/tools` | List the MCP tools the assistant can call |
| `/clear` | Reset conversation history (keeps connection) |
| `/exit` | Quit the session (also `/quit`) |

### /connect wizard

`/connect` walks you through configuring your LLM provider interactively:

1. **Provider** — choose `openai`, `anthropic`, `local`, or `other`
2. **Base URL** — preset filled for known providers; override freely
3. **API key** — input is hidden via `getpass`
4. **Model** — sensible default per provider
5. **MCP URL** — defaults to the current value
6. **Save to profile?** — writes `~/.config/agentic-odi/llm_profile.json` so settings persist across sessions

The wizard can be cancelled at any step with Ctrl-C.

> [!NOTE]
> Chat is the only CLI mode that needs an LLM endpoint. The `customer-outcomes`
> and `connectors` commands keep working without one.

## Manage Jobs, Steps, and desired Outcomes

Every ODI entity has the same create/read/update/delete surface in the CLI and
the MCP server. Jobs hold Steps (the Job Map) and desired Outcomes; deleting a
Job cascades to both.

```bash
# Jobs
agentic-odi jobs add --name "Onboard a customer" --description "First 30 days"
agentic-odi jobs list
agentic-odi jobs get <job-id>
agentic-odi jobs update <job-id> --name "Onboard a new customer"
agentic-odi jobs delete <job-id> --yes

# Steps (Job Map)
agentic-odi steps add --job-id <job-id> --name "Prepare environment" --order 1
agentic-odi steps list --job-id <job-id>
agentic-odi steps get <step-id>
agentic-odi steps update <step-id> --order 2
agentic-odi steps delete <step-id> --yes

# Desired Outcomes
agentic-odi desired-outcomes add --job-id <job-id>   --statement "Minimize the time it takes to get a working environment"   --importance 8 --satisfaction 4
agentic-odi desired-outcomes list --job-id <job-id>
agentic-odi desired-outcomes get <outcome-id>
agentic-odi desired-outcomes update <outcome-id> --satisfaction 6
agentic-odi desired-outcomes delete <outcome-id> --yes
```

Add `--json` to any command for machine-readable output.

## Evidence

Evidence is research captured from connectors (or entered by hand) and linked to
a Job, Step, or desired Outcome. Records can later be promoted into ODI
artifacts — the bridge from research to the model, without hand-copying.

```bash
# Capture a record by hand
agentic-odi evidence add \
  --source-name "interview" --source-kind manual \
  --name "Support lead" \
  --content "Setup takes two days for every new engineer" \
  --job-id <job-id>

# Read and delete
agentic-odi evidence list --job-id <job-id>
agentic-odi evidence list --job-id <job-id> --json
agentic-odi evidence get <evidence-id>
agentic-odi evidence delete <evidence-id> --yes

# Promote into the ODI model
agentic-odi evidence promote <evidence-id> --to job
agentic-odi evidence promote <evidence-id> --to outcome --job-id <job-id>
```

`connectors ingest --job-id <job-id>` maps every evidence-bearing record in the
ingested batch into evidence in one step.

## Schema, scoring, and guidance

```bash
agentic-odi schema            # canonical JSON schema for every ODI entity
agentic-odi score 8 2         # ODI opportunity score → 14.00
agentic-odi evaluate "Minimize the time to ship when onboarding"  # outcome-format check
agentic-odi evaluate --json "Minimize the time to ship when onboarding"
agentic-odi guidelines        # the ODI stage-by-stage guide
agentic-odi capabilities      # what the assistant can do
```

`evaluate` returns the same verdict the `evaluate_outcome` MCP tool does, so the
check works with or without a running server.

## Manage Customer Outcomes

Customer Outcomes link customer value to business value. The `local` backend
writes to the shared SQLite store with no server required; add `--backend mcp`
to route through a running MCP server (`python -m agentic_odi_mcp_server`). The group is also
available under its historical name `outcomes`.

```bash
# Add a Customer Outcome
agentic-odi customer-outcomes add --job-id <job-id> \
  --direction minimize --unit "time" --object "to resolve setup errors" \
  --statement "Minimize the time to resolve environment setup errors when onboarding" \
  --importance 8.8 --satisfaction 3.2 \
  --category cost_reduction \
  --business-statement "Saves engineering hours and reduces early churn"

# Attach value metrics: repeatable JSON objects
agentic-odi customer-outcomes add --job-id <job-id> \
  --direction minimize --unit "time" --object "to resolve setup errors" \
  --statement "Minimize the time to resolve environment setup errors when onboarding" \
  --importance 8.8 --satisfaction 3.2 --category cost_reduction \
  --business-statement "Saves engineering hours" \
  --value-metric '{"name":"first response","direction":"minimize","unit_of_measure":"minutes","importance":7,"satisfaction":3}'

# List outcomes (optionally filtered, or as JSON)
agentic-odi customer-outcomes list
agentic-odi customer-outcomes list --job-id <job-id>
agentic-odi customer-outcomes list --json

# Get, update, delete
agentic-odi customer-outcomes get <outcome-id>
agentic-odi customer-outcomes update <outcome-id> --importance 9.0
agentic-odi customer-outcomes delete <outcome-id> --yes

# Compute an ODI Opportunity Score (top-level, also under the group)
agentic-odi score 8 2
agentic-odi outcomes score 8 2
```

`score` applies the ODI opportunity formula,
`importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0)`.

Set `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` (or `--mcp-url`) to point to a non-default server when
using `--backend mcp` (default: `http://localhost:8000/mcp`).

## Connectors

The `connectors` group manages external MCP integrations. See
[External Connectors](connectors.md) for presets, the connector registry, and
ingest behavior.

```bash
python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors catalog
python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors add mcp --preset github
python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors list
python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors health --name github
python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors ingest --name github
```

## Updates

`odi update` checks for and installs a new binary release. Auto-update is on by
default; disable it with `--no-update` for one run or
`AGENTIC_ODI_NO_UPDATE=1` globally. See [Installation](installation.md).

```

Closes #84"

--- .agents/rules/agent_instructions.md	
+++ .agents/rules/agent_instructions.md	
@@ -1,207 +1,247 @@
 # Agentic ODI - AI Developer Guardrails
 
 This file provides system instructions and guardrails for any AI agents (or LLMs) assisting with the development of the **Agentic ODI** project. Please adhere to these guidelines to maintain consistency and align with the project's vision.
 
 > **Source of Truth for ODI Methodology**: `docs/reference/Strategyn_what_is_Outcome_Driven_Innovation.pdf` by Anthony W. Ulwick (Strategyn). All ODI concepts in this project are grounded in that document. When in doubt, refer agents back to its definitions.
 
 ---
 
 ## 🎯 ODI Methodology Guardrails
 
 This section defines how agents MUST understand and apply Outcome-Driven Innovation within this project. These are not implementation guidelines — they are domain constraints that ensure the system reflects the ODI methodology correctly.
 
 ### What is Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI)?
 
 ODI is a strategy and innovation process rooted in the **Jobs-to-be-Done (JTBD)** theory. Its core premise is: **people buy products and services to get a "job" done**. A "job" is the functional process a person is trying to execute — it remains stable over time, while products and technologies are point-in-time solutions that eventually become obsolete.
 
 ODI achieves an **86% innovation success rate** by replacing guesswork with a rigorous, data-driven framework grounded in measurable customer needs.
 
 ---
 
 ### Stage 1: Define the Market and the Job-to-be-Done
 
 - A **market** is defined as: **a group of people + the functional job they are trying to get done** (e.g., "parents trying to pass on life lessons to children").
 - A **Job-to-be-Done** is the core functional unit of analysis. It is NOT a product, solution, or feature — it is a stable human goal.
 - **Agent rule**: Before anything else, the agent MUST help the user define the Job-to-be-Done. If no Job exists, use `add_job` to capture it. If one exists already, use `get_jobs()` to check first.
 - ❌ **Never skip this stage**. No outcomes, steps, or scoring can be meaningful without a well-defined Job.
 
 ---
 
 ### Stage 2: Uncover Desired Outcomes
 
 - **Desired outcomes** are the metrics customers use to measure success when getting a job done. They are the "needs" in ODI.
 - Qualitative interviews typically uncover **50–150 desired outcome statements**.
 - **Correct outcome statement format** (must be enforced when capturing user input):
 
   > `[Direction] + [Unit of Measure] + [Object of Control] + [Contextual Clarifier]`
 
   - ✅ **Good**: *"Minimize the time it takes to determine if the corn seeds are germinating."*
   - ✅ **Good**: *"Minimize the likelihood of damaging the surface when cutting."*
   - ❌ **Bad**: *"Make it faster"* — too vague, no direction, no measurable unit.
   - ❌ **Bad**: *"I want a notification"* — this is a solution/feature, not an outcome.
 
 - **Agent rule**: Guide the user to express outcomes using this exact format. Reject or reframe vague statements before calling `add_outcome`. Always capture `importance` and `satisfaction` scores (1–10 scale) to enable opportunity scoring.
 
 ---
 
 ### Stage 3: Inventory the Job (Universal Job Map)
 
 - All functional jobs decompose into **8 universal process steps** (the Universal Job Map):
   1. **Define** — Plan what needs to be done; select goals or resources
   2. **Locate** — Gather the inputs, information, or resources needed
   3. **Prepare** — Set up and organize everything required
   4. **Confirm** — Validate readiness; decide whether to proceed
   5. **Execute** — Perform the core task
   6. **Monitor** — Verify and track performance while executing
   7. **Modify** — Adjust or update based on feedback
   8. **Conclude** — Store, finish, or dispose of outputs
 
 - **Agent rule**: When a user is decomposing a job into steps, reference these 8 universal stages as a guide. Steps captured via `add_step` should map to or be inspired by these universal phases. Use `get_job_map` to visualize the ordered structure.
 - ❌ **Do not build the Job Map before capturing outcome statements** — outcomes define *what success looks like*; the job map defines *where in the process* that success matters.
 
 ---
 
 ### Stage 4: Discover Where the Market is Underserved (Opportunity Scoring)
 
 - Each desired outcome is rated by customers on two dimensions:
   - **Importance** (1–10): How important is this outcome to the customer?
   - **Satisfaction** (1–10): How satisfied are customers with current solutions?
 
 - **Opportunity Algorithm** (must be implemented correctly):
 
   ```
   Opportunity Score = Importance + Max(Importance - Satisfaction, 0)
   ```
 
 - **Interpretation**:
   - **Score > 10**: Underserved need — significant innovation opportunity.
   - **Score 10**: Appropriately served — maintain, don't over-invest.
   - **Score < 10**: Overserved — potential for disruption via lower-cost alternatives.
 
 - **Agent rule**: Always compute and surface the opportunity score when both `importance` and `satisfaction` are provided. Highlight outcomes scoring **> 10** as the highest priority innovation targets. Use `get_outcomes(job_id)` to review the full opportunity landscape.
 
 ---
 
 ### Stage 5: Outcome-Based Market Segmentation
 
 - ODI does **not** use demographic segmentation (age, gender, region). Instead it segments the market by **which outcomes are underserved** for each group.
 - Segments can be:
   - **Underserved** — high opportunity scores, want more from existing products
   - **Overserved** — over-investing in outcomes that aren't critical; target for disruption
   - **Appropriately served** — satisfied; maintain current value
 
 - **Agent rule**: When the user has collected outcomes with scores, help them identify outcome clusters that represent distinct market segments. This drives targeted innovation strategy.
 
 ---
 
 ### Stage 6: Formulate an Innovation Strategy
 
 Based on the opportunity analysis, there are three strategic paths:
 
 | Strategy | When to use |
 |---|---|
 | **Differentiated** | Improve existing products to address high-opportunity underserved outcomes |
 | **Disruptive** | Create low-cost solutions for overserved segments that don't need all existing features |
 | **New-Market** | Design products for a new job that is entirely unaddressed |
 
 - **Agent rule**: When the opportunity landscape is clear (outcomes scored, segments identified), guide the user to select a strategy path and align their innovation roadmap accordingly.
 
 ---
 
 ### ⚠️ ODI Behavioral Guardrails for the Agent
 
 These are absolute constraints the agent must respect:
 
 | DO | DON'T |
 |---|---|
 | Always start by defining or confirming the Job-to-be-Done | Jump to solutions, features, or product ideas before the job is defined |
 | Guide outcome statements with the correct format | Accept vague or solution-framed statements as valid outcomes |
 | Compute opportunity scores when importance + satisfaction are available | Skip scoring or calculate it incorrectly |
 | Reference the Universal Job Map when decomposing jobs | Invent arbitrary step structures disconnected from the 8 universal stages |
 | Use outcome-based logic to identify market segments | Use demographics or assumptions to segment the market |
 | Treat outcomes as stable, measurable success metrics | Confuse outcomes with features, preferences, or solutions |
 | Call `get_odi_framework_guidelines` when stage guidance is needed | Guess at which stage comes next |
 
 ---
 
 ## 🛠 Technology Stack & Tools
 - **Language**: Python 3.10+
 - **MCP Framework**: `fastmcp` (Server and Client)
 - **ASGI Server**: `uvicorn`
 - **HTTP Client**: `httpx`
 - **UI / Chat Client**: React + Vite (`apps/studio`), FastAPI sidecar (`apps/studio-api`)
 - **LLM Client**: `openai` (OpenAI-compatible, used with Ollama locally)
 - **Concurrency**: `asyncio`
 - **Data Modeling / Validation**: `pydantic`

 ## 📄 README Maintenance Guardrail
 
 `README.md` is the **primary human-facing entry point** for this project: a short,
 high-level front door aimed at both users and developers. Detailed material lives
 in `docs/` and is linked from the README. The agent MUST keep both current at all
 times.
 
 ### When to update
 
 Update the relevant file whenever any of the following change:
 
 | Change type | Where to update |
 |---|---|
 | New or removed Python file / package | `README.md` **Code Overview** |
 | New dependency added (`pip install ...`) | `README.md` **Quick Start → Prerequisites** |
 | New way to run the project | `README.md` **Quick Start** and `docs/living-studio.md` |
 | New MCP tool or capability | `README.md` **Code Overview** / relevant doc |
 | New CLI command or flag | `docs/cli.md` |
 | New connector kind | `docs/connectors.md` |
 | New workflow or agent instruction | `docs/living-studio.md` |
+| New message part or conversation capability | `docs/living-studio.md` (conversation runtime) |
 | Deployment URL or cloud setup changes | `docs/deployment.md` |
 | Roadmap item completed or added | `docs/roadmap.md` |
 | Test layout or coverage changes | `docs/development.md` |
 
 ### Rules
 
 - ✅ **Update docs in the same task** as the change that triggered it — never defer to a follow-up.
 - ✅ **Keep README short**: it stays a high-level orientation page. Push detail into `docs/` and link to it rather than growing the README.
+- ✅ **Optimize the first five seconds**: the top of the README carries the one-line value proposition and two distinct calls to action — try the hosted Living Studio, or run the full stack locally. Keep the `curl … install.sh | sh` one-liner in the hero.
+- ✅ **Use the fixed section order**: `Why this exists` → `What you get` → `How it works` → `Quick Start` → `Connect your agent` → `Documentation` → `Code Overview` → `Contributing`. Prose sections stay bulleted and skimmable.
 - ✅ **Keep the Quick Start accurate**: always reflect `uv run python scripts/dev.py` as the recommended launch command.
 - ✅ **Keep Prerequisites up to date**: add any new `pip install` dependency immediately.
 - ✅ **Mark Roadmap items `[x]` when completed** — do not leave stale unchecked items.
 - ❌ **Never leave the README or `docs/` in a stale state** where documented commands or files no longer match the codebase.
 
 ---
 
 ## 🚧 Core Development Guardrails
 
 ### 1. Model Context Protocol (MCP) Implementation
 - **Library Choice**: ALWAYS use [`fastmcp`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) for building the MCP architecture. Avoid using the lower-level Anthropic `mcp` SDK directly unless there is a hyper-specific edge case that `fastmcp` does not support.
 - **Transport Protocol**: The project is currently prototyping with **HTTP transport** (not stdio). 
   - The server should be initialized using `mcp.run(transport="http", ...)`.
   - The client must connect to the HTTP endpoint (e.g., `http://localhost:8000/mcp`).
 - **Tool Creation**: 
   - Register tools on the server using the `@mcp.tool` decorator.
   - **CRITICAL**: Provide comprehensive docstrings and strict Python type hints for every tool parameter. Explain exactly what the tool does and what data it expects, as this metadata is fed directly to the LLM for tool discovery.
   - **Contract Synchronization**: Whenever you add, modify, or remove an MCP tool in `apps/mcp-server/src/agentic_odi_mcp_server/mcp_server.py`, you **MUST** simultaneously update `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/contract.py` (`ToolName`, `TOOL_SPECS`) and the `get_capabilities` return string. `tests/contract/test_mcp_contract.py` enforces the surface.
 
 ### 2. Async / Client Practices
 - Use `asyncio` for client execution and IO-bound tool operations.
 - Always use the `fastmcp.Client` securely within an asynchronous context manager (`async with client:`) to ensure connections are efficiently managed and closed.
 
 ### 3. Data Schema & Persistence (ODI Domain)
 - Define all Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) entities (e.g., *Jobs*, *Steps*, *Desired Outcomes*, *Opportunity Scores*) using `pydantic` models.
 - When expanding the server to accept complex payloads or to query data, utilize these Pydantic models for built-in type validation and schema enforcement before the server processes the request.
 
 ### 4. General Philosophy
 - **Separation of Concerns**: Isolate the ODI data logic/retrieval from the MCP server tooling logic.
 - **Agentic Purpose**: Remember that the tools being built are meant to be consumed by autonomous agents. Design tool interfaces that are intuitive for an LLM to call and interpret.
 - **External connectors**: Integrations live in the `packages/connectors` workspace package. New kinds implement `agentic_odi_connectors.protocol.Connector` and register via `register_kind`. Do not write ingested records into `jobs_db` / outcomes unless a later mapping task says so.
 - **MCP client vs ODI server**: The ODI FastMCP **server** exposes product tools. The MCP **client connector** uses `fastmcp.Client` over HTTP to ingest data from *external* MCP servers. Prefer in-memory `Client(server)` tests for that connector, same as server tests.
 
-### 5. Testing Strategy (FastMCP)
+### 5. Conversation UI (assistant-ui)
+
+The Studio's transcript is [assistant-ui](https://www.assistant-ui.com) bound to
+our own store; it is not a hand-rolled message list. Do not replace it, wrap it in
+a second one, or re-implement streaming, the composer, attachments, branches, or
+approval prompts beside it.
+
+- **One bridge.** `apps/studio/src/assistant/convert.ts` is the only mapping
+  between `ChatMessage`/`ChatPart` and assistant-ui parts. It is pure and tested
+  without a runtime. A new part type is added there, rendered in `parts.tsx`, and
+  registered in the `components` map in `Conversation.tsx` — three files, never a
+  fourth path.
+- **The store stays ours.** `state/StudioContext.tsx` owns messages, ids,
+  `parentId`, streaming state, memory, and canvas invalidation. The runtime is
+  presentation: `useExternalStoreRuntime` in `assistant/StudioRuntime.tsx` maps
+  `onNew`, `onEdit`, `onReload`, `onCancel`, `setMessages`, and
+  `onRespondToToolApproval` onto context actions. Do not let component state
+  become a second source of truth.
+- **The SSE contract stays additive.** The sidecar is a Python tool loop; it is
+  not migrating to Vercel's AI SDK stream protocol. New capability arrives as a
+  new event (`reasoning`, `source`, `approval`, `ui`, …) or a new opt-in request
+  field, and a client that sends neither must see the old stream unchanged.
+- **The ODI catalog stays ours.** Generated surfaces travel as assistant-ui
+  `data-*` parts and render through `UiRenderer`. assistant-ui's generic
+  generative-UI vocabulary is not a replacement for the server-validated catalog.
+- **No fabricated provenance.** A source names what a turn actually read; a part
+  the converter does not understand is dropped, never printed as JSON.
+- **Approvals gate writes, not reads.** `approvals: true` pauses mutating tools
+  only; the gate is in-process, single-user, timeout-bound, and resolving a gate
+  twice must not run a tool twice.
+- **Voice is a seam, not a feature.** It is deliberately deferred: `adapters.dictation`
+  plus `ComposerPrimitive.Dictate`, no backend change. Do not ship a microphone
+  that only works in the browser shell.
+- **Keep it honest in the docs.** A capability that lands here is described in
+  `docs/living-studio.md` → *The conversation runtime*, with its test in
+  `docs/development.md`, in the same change.
+
+### 6. Testing Strategy (FastMCP)
 - **First-Class Documentation**: Treat tests as living documentation that demonstrate how features work while protecting against regressions.
 - **Speed & Isolation**: Tests must be fast (< 1s) and self-contained. Use `@pytest.mark.integration` or `@pytest.mark.client_process` for slower, integration, or resource-dependent tests.
 - **Structure**: This repo is a uv workspace. Mirror each project's code structure in its own `tests/` directory (e.g., `apps/mcp-server/src/agentic_odi_mcp_server/mcp_server.py` -> `apps/mcp-server/tests/test_server_tools.py`, `packages/connectors/src/agentic_odi_connectors/mcp/connector.py` -> `packages/connectors/tests/test_mcp_connector.py`).
 - **Atomic Tests**: Each test must verify exactly one specific behavior with clear intent in test names and assertions. Avoid multi-behavior tests.
 - **In-Memory Testing (Preferred)**: Favor testing functionality deterministically by passing the `FastMCP` server directly into the `Client(server)` instance. This runs in-memory without network overhead for deterministic and lightning-fast execution.
 - **Transport Testing (When Needed)**: For HTTP/SSE network transport tests, prefer the isolated in-process `fastmcp.utilities.tests.run_server_async(server)` context manager over subprocess testing (which uses `run_server_in_process` and is slower to debug).
 - **Data Assertions**: Utilize `inline-snapshot` (`snapshot()`) for assessing complex data structures like tool API JSON schemas or expected responses.

Index: .github/actions/pr-risk/score.sh
===================================================================
--- .github/actions/pr-risk/score.sh	
+++ .github/actions/pr-risk/score.sh	
@@ -0,0 +1,186 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+#
+# score.sh — Native GitHub Action PR risk classifier.
+#
+# Evaluates a pull request diff across three factors and applies a single,
+# mutually exclusive risk label. Runs entirely on ubuntu-latest with git + gh
+# (both preinstalled on GitHub-hosted runners). Zero external SaaS, zero API
+# keys, zero PR comments.
+#
+# Factors (0-100 score):
+#   1. File & line churn        -> 0-30 points
+#   2. Critical path override   -> forces danger zone (>= 51)
+#   3. Test delta               -> +20 if source changed without test files
+#
+# Tiers:
+#   <= 20  -> safe to merge     (🟢)
+#   21-50  -> needs a look      (🟡)
+#   >= 51  -> danger zone       (🔴)
+#
+# Env required: GITHUB_TOKEN, BASE_SHA, HEAD_SHA, PR_NUMBER, REPO
+
+set -euo pipefail
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Configuration
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+readonly RISK_LABELS=("safe to merge" "needs a look" "danger zone")
+readonly CRITICAL_PREFIXES=("auth/" "migrations/" "billing/" "infra/" ".github/workflows/")
+readonly PROTECTED_FILES_FILE=".ci/protected-files.txt"
+
+# Score thresholds
+readonly CHURN_FILES_MAX=10      # points
+readonly CHURN_LINES_MAX=20      # points
+readonly CHURN_LINES_CAP=400     # lines at which line-points saturate
+readonly TEST_DELTA_POINTS=20
+readonly DANGER_FLOOR=51
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Helpers
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+# Returns 0 (true) if $1 is a test file: *.test.*, *.spec.*, or under tests/
+is_test_file() {
+  local f="$1"
+  [[ "${f}" == *.test.* || "${f}" == *.spec.* ]] && return 0
+  [[ "${f}" == tests/* || "${f}" == */tests/* ]] && return 0
+  return 1
+}
+
+# Returns 0 (true) if $1 is source code worth test coverage (excludes docs,
+# configs, static assets, lockfiles, etc.). Test delta only fires on these.
+is_source_file() {
+  local f="$1"
+  local ext="${f##*.}"
+  case "${ext}" in
+    py|ts|tsx|js|jsx|go|rs|rb|java|c|cpp|h|hpp|cs|php|swift|kt|scala|r|m|mm|sh|bash|zsh|tf|vue|dart|lua|ex|exs|erl|hs|ml|clj|cljs|sql|graphql|proto) return 0 ;;
+  esac
+  local base="${f##*/}"
+  case "${base}" in
+    Dockerfile|dockerfile|Makefile|makefile|Gemfile|Rakefile|Vagrantfile|BUILD|BUILD.bazel|WORKSPACE|configure|Configure) return 0 ;;
+  esac
+  return 1
+}
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Gather diff between base and head
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+# All changed files (Added / Copied / Modified / Deleted)
+CHANGED_FILES="$(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=ACMD "${BASE_SHA}" "${HEAD_SHA}" || true)"
+
+# Shortstat for churn counts
+STAT="$(git diff --shortstat "${BASE_SHA}" "${HEAD_SHA}" || true)"
+
+FILES_CHANGED_COUNT=0
+LINES_ADDED=0
+LINES_DELETED=0
+if [[ -n "${STAT}" ]]; then
+  FILES_CHANGED_COUNT="$(printf '%s' "${STAT}" | grep -oE '[0-9]+ file' | grep -oE '[0-9]+' || echo 0)"
+  LINES_ADDED="$(printf '%s' "${STAT}" | grep -oE '[0-9]+ insertion' | grep -oE '[0-9]+' || echo 0)"
+  LINES_DELETED="$(printf '%s' "${STAT}" | grep -oE '[0-9]+ deletion' | grep -oE '[0-9]+' || echo 0)"
+fi
+[[ -z "${FILES_CHANGED_COUNT}" ]] && FILES_CHANGED_COUNT=0
+[[ -z "${LINES_ADDED}" ]] && LINES_ADDED=0
+[[ -z "${LINES_DELETED}" ]] && LINES_DELETED=0
+readonly TOTAL_LINES=$((LINES_ADDED + LINES_DELETED))
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Factor 1: File & line churn (0-30)
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+score=0
+
+# Files changed: 1 point per file, capped at CHURN_FILES_MAX
+if [[ "${FILES_CHANGED_COUNT}" -ge "${CHURN_FILES_MAX}" ]]; then
+  churn_files="${CHURN_FILES_MAX}"
+else
+  churn_files="${FILES_CHANGED_COUNT}"
+fi
+score=$((score + churn_files))
+
+# Lines changed: linear up to CHURN_LINES_MAX at CHURN_LINES_CAP lines
+if [[ "${TOTAL_LINES}" -ge "${CHURN_LINES_CAP}" ]]; then
+  churn_lines="${CHURN_LINES_MAX}"
+else
+  churn_lines=$((TOTAL_LINES * CHURN_LINES_MAX / CHURN_LINES_CAP))
+  [[ "${churn_lines}" -gt "${CHURN_LINES_MAX}" ]] && churn_lines="${CHURN_LINES_MAX}"
+fi
+score=$((score + churn_lines))
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Factor 2: Critical path override (blast radius)
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+critical_touch=0
+
+while IFS= read -r f; do
+  [[ -z "${f}" ]] && continue
+  for prefix in "${CRITICAL_PREFIXES[@]}"; do
+    if [[ "${f}" == "${prefix}"* ]]; then
+      critical_touch=1
+      break 2
+    fi
+  done
+done <<< "${CHANGED_FILES}"
+
+# Deletions of protected CI/site files also count as critical.
+if [[ -f "${PROTECTED_FILES_FILE}" && -n "${CHANGED_FILES}" ]]; then
+  while IFS= read -r f; do
+    [[ -z "${f}" ]] && continue
+    # Only consider deletions: a file in the diff that no longer exists at HEAD
+    if ! git cat-file -e "${HEAD_SHA}:${f}" 2>/dev/null; then
+      while IFS= read -r p; do
+        [[ -z "${p}" || "${p}" == \#* ]] && continue
+        if [[ "${f}" == "${p}" ]]; then
+          critical_touch=1
+          break 2
+        fi
+      done < "${PROTECTED_FILES_FILE}"
+    fi
+  done <<< "${CHANGED_FILES}"
+fi
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Factor 3: Test delta (+20 if source changed without test files)
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+source_changed=0
+test_changed=0
+
+while IFS= read -r f; do
+  [[ -z "${f}" ]] && continue
+  if is_test_file "${f}"; then
+    test_changed=1
+  elif is_source_file "${f}"; then
+    source_changed=1
+  fi
+done <<< "${CHANGED_FILES}"
+
+if [[ "${source_changed}" -eq 1 && "${test_changed}" -eq 0 ]]; then
+  score=$((score + TEST_DELTA_POINTS))
+fi
+
+# Apply critical-path floor
+if [[ "${critical_touch}" -eq 1 && "${score}" -lt "${DANGER_FLOOR}" ]]; then
+  score="${DANGER_FLOOR}"
+fi
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Determine tier (mutually exclusive)
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+if [[ "${score}" -le 20 ]]; then
+  tier="safe to merge"
+elif [[ "${score}" -le 50 ]]; then
+  tier="needs a look"
+else
+  tier="danger zone"
+fi
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Label hygiene: remove all stale risk labels, then apply the current tier.
+# No PR comments are posted (silent execution).
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+for label in "${RISK_LABELS[@]}"; do
+  gh pr edit "${PR_NUMBER}" --repo "${REPO}" --remove-label "${label}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+done
+gh pr edit "${PR_NUMBER}" --repo "${REPO}" --add-label "${tier}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+
+echo "PR risk score: ${score}/100 -> ${tier}"

--- .github/workflows/chromatic.yml	
+++ .github/workflows/chromatic.yml	
@@ -0,0 +1,73 @@
+name: Chromatic
+
+# Chromatic recommends the push event over pull_request. A pull_request run
+# checks out an ephemeral merge commit, so the branch's history no longer holds
+# main's latest commits and the diff would include everything merged since the
+# branch point. A push build diffs the branch's own commits against the
+# baseline; Chromatic still reports its "UI Tests" check on the pull request
+# that contains the commit. Tags are excluded because they have no baseline.
+on:
+  push:
+    branches: ["**"]
+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+# A newer push supersedes the previous build for the same branch.
+concurrency:
+  group: chromatic-${{ github.ref }}
+  cancel-in-progress: true
+
+defaults:
+  run:
+    shell: bash
+
+jobs:
+  chromatic:
+    name: Visual tests (Chromatic)
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 20
+    defaults:
+      run:
+        working-directory: apps/studio
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          # Chromatic walks git history to find the baseline build to diff against.
+          fetch-depth: 0
+
+      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
+        with:
+          node-version: "lts/*"
+          cache: npm
+          cache-dependency-path: apps/studio/package-lock.json
+
+      - name: Install dependencies
+        run: npm ci
+
+      - name: Install Chromium for Vitest Browser Mode
+        run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
+
+      # The test run is itself the check: a component that renders an error
+      # fails the workflow before any snapshot is billed.
+      - name: Capture component snapshots
+        run: npm run test:visual
+
+      # Fork branches never reach this workflow (it runs in this repository),
+      # and Dependabot pushes cannot read repository secrets. Every other run
+      # has to publish, because a green check with no build would hide broken
+      # wiring instead of verifying the UI.
+      - name: Publish to Chromatic
+        env:
+          CHROMATIC_PROJECT_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CHROMATIC_PROJECT_TOKEN }}
+        run: |
+          if [ -z "$CHROMATIC_PROJECT_TOKEN" ]; then
+            if [ "$GITHUB_ACTOR" = "dependabot[bot]" ]; then
+              echo "::notice::Dependabot runs cannot read repository secrets, so snapshots were captured but not published."
+              exit 0
+            fi
+            echo "::error::CHROMATIC_PROJECT_TOKEN is not set. Add the Chromatic project token (Manage > Project token) as a repository secret."
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          npm run chromatic

@@ -0,0 +1,74 @@
+name: Label merge conflicts
+
+on:
+  pull_request:
+    branches: [main]
+    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
+  schedule:
+    - cron: '0 */6 * * *'
+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+permissions:
+  contents: write
+  pull-requests: write
+
+concurrency:
+  group: label-merge-conflicts-${{ github.ref }}
+  cancel-in-progress: true
+
+jobs:
+  label-merge-state:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 10
+    steps:
+      - name: Ensure labels exist
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+        run: |
+          gh label create merge-conflict --color b60205 \
+            --description "Pull request has merge conflicts" --force || true
+          gh label create merge-ready --color 28a745 \
+            --description "Pull request merges cleanly into main" --force || true
+
+      - name: Collect target PR numbers
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+        run: |
+          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "pull_request" ]; then
+            echo "${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/pr-numbers.txt"
+          else
+            gh pr list --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --base main \
+              --state open --json number -q '.[].number' \
+              > "$RUNNER_TEMP/pr-numbers.txt"
+          fi
+
+      - name: Label each PR by merge state
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+        run: |
+          while IFS= read -r number; do
+            [ -z "$number" ] && continue
+            state="$(gh pr view "$number" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
+              --json mergeStateStatus -q '.mergeStateStatus')"
+            case "$state" in
+              dirty)
+                gh pr edit "$number" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
+                  --add-label merge-conflict >/dev/null
+                gh pr edit "$number" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
+                  --remove-label merge-ready >/dev/null || true
+                ;;
+              clean)
+                gh pr edit "$number" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
+                  --add-label merge-ready >/dev/null
+                gh pr edit "$number" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
+                  --remove-label merge-conflict >/dev/null || true
+                ;;
+              *)
+                gh pr edit "$number" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
+                  --remove-label merge-conflict >/dev/null || true
+                gh pr edit "$number" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
+                  --remove-label merge-ready >/dev/null || true
+                ;;
+            esac
+            echo "PR #$number: $state"
+          done < "$RUNNER_TEMP/pr-numbers.txt"

+name: PR guardrails
+
+# Deterministic gates that a pull request cannot lie about its shape.
+# No repository secrets: the gates only need the checked-out repository.
+on:
+  pull_request:
+    branches: [main]
+    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, edited]
+
+concurrency:
+  group: pr-guardrails-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
+  cancel-in-progress: true
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+  pull-requests: write
+
+defaults:
+  run:
+    shell: bash
+
+jobs:
+  pr-guardrails:
+    name: PR guardrails
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 10
+    steps:
+      # Full history so the cumulative base...HEAD diff and release tags exist.
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          fetch-depth: 0
+
+      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup
+
+      - name: Fetch the base branch
+        run: |
+          git fetch --no-tags origin \
+            "${{ github.base_ref }}:refs/remotes/origin/${{ github.base_ref }}"
+
+      # The diff-shape gate is the only gate that blocks, and it runs on the
+      # cumulative diff: a tree-replacement commit in the middle of a branch
+      # stays visible here.
+      - name: Diff-shape gate
+        if: always()
+        run: |
+          uv run python scripts/pr_guards.py diff-shape \
+            --base-ref "origin/${{ github.base_ref }}"
+
+      - name: Body-truth gate
+        if: always()
+        env:
+          PR_BODY: ${{ github.event.pull_request.body }}
+          PR_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
+        run: |
+          printf '%s' "$PR_BODY" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/pr-body.md"
+          uv run python scripts/pr_guards.py body-truth \
+            --base-ref "origin/${{ github.base_ref }}" \
+            --body-file "$RUNNER_TEMP/pr-body.md" \
+            --title "$PR_TITLE" \
+            --warnings-out "$RUNNER_TEMP/body-warnings.txt"
+
+      - name: Fabrication guard
+        if: always()
+        run: |
+          uv run python scripts/pr_guards.py fabrication \
+            --base-ref "origin/${{ github.base_ref }}" \
+            --warnings-out "$RUNNER_TEMP/fabrication-warnings.txt"
+
+      - name: Publish guardrail warnings
+        if: always()
+        continue-on-error: true
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
+          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
+          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
+        run: |
+          message="$RUNNER_TEMP/guardrail-warnings.md"
+          : > "$message"
+          for file in "$RUNNER_TEMP/body-warnings.txt" "$RUNNER_TEMP/fabrication-warnings.txt"; do
+            if [ -s "$file" ]; then
+              {
+                echo "## PR guardrails — warnings"
+                echo
+                echo '```'
+                cat "$file"
+                echo '```'
+              } >> "$message"
+            fi
+          done
+          comment_id="$(gh api "repos/$REPO/issues/$PR_NUMBER/comments" --paginate \
+            --jq '.[] | select(.body | startswith("## PR guardrails")) | .id' |
+            head -n 1)"
+          if [ -s "$message" ]; then
+            if [ -n "$comment_id" ]; then
+              gh api --method PATCH "repos/$REPO/issues/comments/$comment_id" \
+                -F body=@"$message" >/dev/null
+            else
+              gh pr comment "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "$REPO" --body-file "$message"
+            fi
+          elif [ -n "$comment_id" ]; then
+            gh api --method DELETE "repos/$REPO/issues/comments/$comment_id" >/dev/null
+          fi

 name: release
 
+# release-please publishes the GitHub release via the API; that emits a
+# `release` event, not a tag push. Both paths are kept so hand-cut tags still

+        uses: ./.github/actions/setup
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.11"

+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          tag_version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
+          reported="$(uv run python -m agentic_odi_cli --version)"
+          # `--version` prints "<version> (<date>)" when a build date is set.
+          cli_version="${reported%% *}"
+          if [ "$cli_version" != "$tag_version" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Tag v${tag_version} does not match the CLI version ${cli_version}. Bump the declared version before tagging."
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          echo "OK: version ${cli_version} matches tag v${tag_version}"

           - os: linux

           - os: linux
             runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
             target: linux_arm64
           - os: macos
             runner: macos-14
             target: macos_arm64
           - os: macos
             runner: macos-15-intel
             target: macos_x86_64
           - os: windows
             runner: windows-latest
             target: windows_x86_64

     # which the manylinux2014 images (glibc 2.17) cannot provide. If a narrower
     # glibc floor is needed later, use a manylinux_2_28 image instead.
     runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
     steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v7
       - name: Setup uv
         uses: ./.github/actions/setup
         with:
           python-version: "3.11"
       - name: Build
         env:
           TARGET: ${{ matrix.target }}
         run: |
           VERSION="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
           RELEASE_DATE_UTC="$(git log -1 --format=%cI)"
           export VERSION RELEASE_DATE_UTC

       - name: Write checksums
         shell: bash
         run: |
           set -euo pipefail
           shopt -s nullglob
           archives=(odi_*.tar.gz odi_*.zip)

             echo "::error::No archive was produced for ${{ matrix.target }}"
             exit 1
           fi

             sha256sum "${archives[@]}" > "checksums-${{ matrix.target }}.txt"
           elif command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
             shasum -a 256 "${archives[@]}" > "checksums-${{ matrix.target }}.txt"
           else

             exit 1
           fi

           name: checksums-${{ matrix.target }}
           path: checksums-${{ matrix.target }}.txt

         uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v3
         with:
           files: |
             odi_*.tar.gz
             odi_*.zip

         with:
           files: |
             scripts/install.sh
             scripts/install.ps1

 name: Tauri Release
 
+# release-please creates the GitHub release through the API, which does not
+# emit a `push` event for the tag. Listening for the published release is what
+# actually starts the desktop build (and therefore publishes latest.json, which
+# the in-app updater depends on). `push` stays for tags created by hand.
+
 on:
   push:
     tags:
       - "v*"
+  release:
+    types: [published]
   workflow_dispatch:
     inputs:
       tag:
         description: "Existing release tag to attach desktop bundles to (e.g. v0.3.0)"
         required: true
         type: string
 
 concurrency:
   group: tauri-release-${{ inputs.tag || github.ref_name }}
   cancel-in-progress: false
 
 permissions:
   contents: write
 
 jobs:
   preflight:
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     timeout-minutes: 10
     steps:
       - name: Require updater signing key
         env:
           SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY }}
         run: |
           if [ -z "$SIGNING_KEY" ]; then
             echo "::error::TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY is required to publish a signed release; without it the updater artifacts would be broken."
             exit 1
           fi
 
   build:
     needs: [preflight]
     strategy:
       fail-fast: false
       matrix:
         include:
           - platform: ubuntu-22.04
             args: ""
           - platform: macos-latest
             args: "--target aarch64-apple-darwin"
           - platform: macos-latest
             args: "--target x86_64-apple-darwin"
           - platform: windows-latest
             args: ""
     runs-on: ${{ matrix.platform }}
     timeout-minutes: 90
     steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v7
 
       - name: Install Linux webview dependencies
         if: matrix.platform == 'ubuntu-22.04'
         run: |
           sudo apt-get update
           sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev build-essential curl wget file \
             libxdo-dev libssl-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf
 
       - name: Setup Rust
         uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
         with:
           targets: ${{ startsWith(matrix.platform, 'macos') && 'aarch64-apple-darwin,x86_64-apple-darwin' || '' }}
 
       - uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2
         with:
           workspaces: apps/studio/src-tauri -> target
 
       - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
         with:
           node-version: "lts/*"
           cache: npm
           cache-dependency-path: apps/studio/package-lock.json
 
       - name: Install frontend dependencies
         run: npm ci
         working-directory: apps/studio
 
       - name: Import Windows signing certificate
         if: matrix.platform == 'windows-latest'
         shell: pwsh
         env:
           WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE: ${{ secrets.WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE }}
           WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD }}
         run: |
           if ([string]::IsNullOrEmpty($env:WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE)) {
             Write-Output "No WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE secret — building unsigned Windows installer."
             exit 0

           $path = Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP "cert.pfx"

           $secure = ConvertTo-SecureString -String $env:WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD -AsPlainText -Force
           $cert = Import-PfxCertificate -FilePath $path -CertStoreLocation Cert:\CurrentUser\My -Password $secure
           $config = '{"bundle":{"windows":{"certificateThumbprint":"' + $cert.Thumbprint + '"}}}'
           "TAURI_CONFIG=$config" | Out-File -FilePath $env:GITHUB_ENV -Append -Encoding utf8
           Write-Output "Imported Windows certificate $($cert.Thumbprint)"

       # attaches the desktop bundles to it and publishes it — no draft is left
       # behind for a maintainer to publish by hand.
       - name: Build and attach release
         uses: tauri-apps/tauri-action@v1
         env:
           GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
           TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY }}
           TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD }}

           APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD }}
           APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY: ${{ secrets.APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY }}
           APPLE_ID: ${{ secrets.APPLE_ID }}

           projectPath: apps/studio

           releaseDraft: false
           prerelease: false
           args: ${{ matrix.args }}
+
+  # A release without a usable latest.json cannot update anybody. Fail the
+  # release loudly instead of leaving a quiet download that installs nothing.
+  verify:
+    needs: [build]
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 10
+    steps:
+      - name: Verify the signed updater manifest covers every platform
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+          TAG: ${{ inputs.tag || github.ref_name }}
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          version="${TAG#v}"
+          dir="$(mktemp -d)"
+          for attempt in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do
+            if gh release download "$TAG" --pattern latest.json --dir "$dir" --clobber; then
+              break
+            fi
+            echo "latest.json not available yet (attempt $attempt); retrying…"
+            sleep 10
+          done
+          manifest="$dir/latest.json"
+          if [ ! -f "$manifest" ]; then
+            echo "::error::latest.json was not published for $TAG, so installed apps cannot update."
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          manifest_version="$(jq -r '.version // empty' "$manifest")"
+          if [ "$manifest_version" != "$version" ]; then
+            echo "::error::latest.json advertises $manifest_version but the tag is $version."
+            echo "The desktop app version is out of sync with the release; see the release-please extra-files config."
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          for key in linux-x86_64 windows-x86_64 darwin-aarch64 darwin-x86_64; do
+            if ! jq -e --arg k "$key" '.platforms[$k].url and .platforms[$k].signature' "$manifest" > /dev/null; then
+              echo "::error::latest.json is missing a signed $key artifact."
+              exit 1
+            fi
+          done
+          echo "OK: $TAG publishes a signed updater manifest for every platform"

 @dataclass(frozen=True)
 class ChatConfig:
     """Connection settings for an interactive chat session."""
 
     base_url: str
     api_key: str
     model: str
     mcp_url: str
 
     @classmethod
     def from_env(
         cls,
         *,
         base_url: str | None = None,
         api_key: str | None = None,
         model: str | None = None,
         mcp_url: str | None = None,
     ) -> ChatConfig:
         """Resolve settings in priority order: explicit arg > env var > LLM profile > default."""
         # Lazy import to avoid circular imports between chat and profile.
         from agentic_odi_cli.profile import load_llm_profile  # noqa: PLC0415
 
         try:
             llm_profile = load_llm_profile()
         except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
             llm_profile = None
 
         return cls(
             base_url=(
                 base_url
                 or os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL")
                 or (llm_profile.base_url if llm_profile else None)
                 or DEFAULT_BASE_URL
             ),
             api_key=(
                 api_key
                 or os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY")
                 or (llm_profile.api_key if llm_profile else None)
                 or DEFAULT_API_KEY
             ),
             model=(
                 model
                 or os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL")
                 or (llm_profile.model if llm_profile else None)
                 or DEFAULT_MODEL
             ),
             mcp_url=(
                 mcp_url
                 or os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL")

 @dataclass

     llm_ok: bool = False
     mcp_ok: bool = False
     mcp_tool_count: int = 0
     error_llm: str | None = None

 class ChatSessionLike(Protocol):
     """The session surface the command handler needs."""
 
     tool_names: list[str]
     config: ChatConfig
     connection_state: ConnectionState
 
     def clear(self) -> None: ...
 
     def update_config(self, config: ChatConfig) -> None: ...
 
 
 def _to_openai_tools(tools: list[Any]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
     """Translate FastMCP tool definitions into OpenAI function schemas."""
     return [
         {
             "type": "function",
             "function": {
                 "name": tool.name,
                 "description": tool.description or "",
                 "parameters": tool.input_schema or {"type": "object", "properties": {}},
             },
         }
         for tool in tools
     ]
 
 
 def _normalize_tool_calls(entries: dict[int, dict[str, str]]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
     """Turn the per-index streaming tool-call buffers into OpenAI tool calls."""
     return [
         {
             "id": entry["id"] or f"call_{index}",
             "type": "function",
             "function": {
                 "name": entry["name"],
                 "arguments": entry["arguments"] or "{}",
             },
         }
         for index, entry in entries.items()
     ]
 
 
 def _tool_result_text(result: Any) -> str:
     """Extract readable text from an MCP tool result."""
     content = getattr(result, "content", None) or []
     parts = [getattr(item, "text", None) for item in content]
     text = "\n".join(part for part in parts if part)
     return text or str(result)
 
 
 def handle_command(
     line: str,
     session: ChatSessionLike,
     *,
     on_connect: Callable[[], ChatConfig | None] | None = None,
     on_mcp_reconnect: Callable[[str], bool] | None = None,
 ) -> Literal["exit", "handled"] | tuple[str, str] | None:
     """Handle a slash command, or return None when the line is a chat message.
 
     Returns:
         "exit"              — caller should end the session.
         "handled"           — command was handled; continue the REPL.
         ("reconnect_mcp", url) — caller should reconnect MCP then continue.
         None                — not a command; caller should send to the LLM.
     """
     command = line.strip().lower()
     if command in {"/exit", "/quit"}:
         return "exit"
     if command == "/help":
         typer.echo(HELP_TEXT)
         return "handled"
     if command == "/clear":
         session.clear()
         typer.echo("Conversation cleared.")
         return "handled"
     if command == "/tools":
         if session.tool_names:
             typer.echo("\n".join(session.tool_names))
         else:
             typer.echo("No tools loaded.")
         return "handled"
     if command == "/status":
         state = session.connection_state
         llm_status = "connected" if state.llm_ok else "not connected"
         mcp_status = (
             f"connected ({state.mcp_tool_count} tools)" if state.mcp_ok else "not connected"

     """Re-exec into the freshly installed binary (POSIX only)."""
     current = paths.current_link()
     binary = current / "odi"
     can_exec = (
         os.name == "posix" and hasattr(os, "execv") and current.is_symlink() and binary.exists()

         typer.echo("Update applied; it will take effect on the next run.")

     argv = sys.argv[1:]

     """Check for or apply CLI updates."""
     if check:
         latest = update.latest_release(__version__)
         if latest is None:

         else:
             typer.echo(f"Update available: v{latest} - run 'odi update' to install.")
         return
 
     if not paths.is_frozen():
         typer.echo("This is a source install; use your package manager to update.")
         return
 
     target = version.lstrip("v") if version else update.latest_release(__version__)
     if target is None:
         if force:
             target = __version__
         else:
             typer.echo(f"Already up to date (v{__version__}).")
             return
 
     try:
         with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="odi-update-") as tmp:
             archive = update.download(target, Path(tmp))
             digest = hashlib.sha256(archive.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
             update.perform_update(target, archive, digest, paths.install_root())
     except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
         typer.echo(f"Update failed: {exc}", err=True)
         raise typer.Exit(code=1) from exc

     if not (sys.stdin.isatty() and sys.stdout.isatty()):

     # Do not trigger onboarding for specific subcommands
     if invoked_subcommand and invoked_subcommand in {"setup", "profile", "version", "help"}:
         return
 
     typer.echo("First-run onboarding card")
     typer.echo("=" * 60)
     for line in CARD_LINES:
         typer.echo(line)
     typer.echo("=" * 60)
     typer.echo("".join(HONESTY_CONTRACT_LINES))
     typer.echo("Run `agentic-odi setup` to configure your product baseline interactively.")
