@@ -0,0 +1,189 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Proves the Living Studio updater end to end against a local release feed:
+#
+#   1. generates a throwaway minisign key
+#   2. builds signed 0.1.0 and 0.2.0 AppImages pointed at a local latest.json
+#   3. runs 0.1.0 and waits for it to install 0.2.0 over its own file
+#   4. runs the result again and asserts it checks, finds nothing, and downloads
+#      nothing
+#
+# This is a manual proof, not part of CI: it builds the desktop shell twice and
+# needs a Linux display plus AppImage/FUSE support. Run it from a workstation:
+#
+#   bash scripts/verify-desktop-update.sh
+#
+# The throwaway key means the built AppImages only trust this test feed; the
+# committed public key is untouched.
+set -euo pipefail
+
+REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
+STUDIO="$REPO_ROOT/apps/studio"
+WORK="${WORK:-/tmp/studio-update-e2e}"
+PORT="${PORT:-8787}"
+OLD_VERSION="0.1.0"
+NEW_VERSION="0.2.0"
+
+APP_PID=""
+SERVER_PID=""
+
+cleanup() {
+  if [ -n "$APP_PID" ] && kill -0 "$APP_PID" 2>/dev/null; then
+    kill "$APP_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
+    wait "$APP_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
+  fi
+  if [ -n "$SERVER_PID" ] && kill -0 "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null; then
+    kill "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
+    wait "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
+  fi
+}
+trap cleanup EXIT
+
+say() { printf '\n\033[1m==> %s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }
+
+rm -rf "$WORK"
+mkdir -p "$WORK/feed" "$WORK/run"
+
+say "Generating a throwaway updater key"
+(
+  cd "$STUDIO"
+  npx tauri signer generate -w "$WORK/updater.key" -p "" -f > /dev/null
+)
+# `tauri signer generate` writes the public key already base64-encoded, which
+# is exactly what `plugins.updater.pubkey` expects.
+PUBKEY="$(tr -d '\n' < "$WORK/updater.key.pub")"
+
+build_appimage() {
+  local version="$1"
+  local config_file="$WORK/config-$version.json"
+
+  python3 - "$version" "$PUBKEY" "$PORT" > "$config_file" <<'PY'
+import json
+import sys
+
+version, pubkey, port = sys.argv[1:4]
+print(json.dumps({
+    "version": version,
+    "plugins": {
+        "updater": {
+            "pubkey": pubkey,
+            "endpoints": [f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/latest.json"],
+            "dangerousInsecureTransportProtocol": True,
+        }
+    },
+}))
+PY
+
+  if [ ! -s "$config_file" ]; then
+    echo "The Tauri config override for $version was not written." >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+
+  rm -f "$STUDIO"/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/appimage/*_"$version"_amd64.AppImage*
+
+  say "Building signed AppImage $version"
+  (
+    cd "$STUDIO"
+    TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY="$WORK/updater.key" \
+      TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD="" \
+      npx tauri build --config "$config_file" --bundles appimage
+  )
+
+  local built
+  built="$(ls "$STUDIO"/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/appimage/*_"$version"_amd64.AppImage)"
+  if [ ! -f "$built.sig" ]; then
+    echo "No updater signature was produced for $version." >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  local target="$WORK/feed/studio-$version.AppImage"
+  cp "$built" "$target"
+  cp "$built.sig" "$target.sig"
+  sha256sum "$target" | awk '{print $1}' > "$WORK/feed/studio-$version.sha256"
+}
+
+build_appimage "$OLD_VERSION"
+build_appimage "$NEW_VERSION"
+
+say "Publishing a local update feed"
+python3 - "$WORK" "$PORT" "$NEW_VERSION" "$OLD_VERSION" <<'PY'
+import json
+import pathlib
+import sys
+
+work, port, version, _old = sys.argv[1:5]
+feed = pathlib.Path(work) / "feed"
+signature = (feed / f"studio-{version}.AppImage.sig").read_text().strip()
+(feed / "latest.json").write_text(json.dumps({
+    "version": version,
+    "notes": "Verifies the in-app updater end to end.",
+    "pub_date": "2026-10-21T00:00:00Z",
+    "platforms": {
+        "linux-x86_64": {
+            "signature": signature,
+            "url": f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/studio-{version}.AppImage",
+        }
+    },
+}, indent=2))
+PY
+
+python3 -m http.server "$PORT" --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory "$WORK/feed" \
+  > "$WORK/server.log" 2>&1 &
+SERVER_PID=$!
+sleep 1
+
+cp "$WORK/feed/studio-$OLD_VERSION.AppImage" "$WORK/run/studio.AppImage"
+chmod +x "$WORK/run/studio.AppImage"
+
+say "Running $OLD_VERSION; it should update itself in the background"
+(
+  cd "$WORK/run"
+  ./studio.AppImage > "$WORK/app.log" 2>&1
+) &
+APP_PID=$!
+
+NEW_SHA="$(cat "$WORK/feed/studio-$NEW_VERSION.sha256")"
+APPLIED=0
+for _ in $(seq 1 90); do
+  CURRENT_SHA="$(sha256sum "$WORK/run/studio.AppImage" | awk '{print $1}')"
+  if [ "$CURRENT_SHA" = "$NEW_SHA" ]; then
+    APPLIED=1
+    break
+  fi
+  sleep 2
+done
+
+if [ "$APPLIED" -ne 1 ]; then
+  echo "The app did not install $NEW_VERSION over itself." >&2
+  echo "--- app log ---" >&2
+  tail -40 "$WORK/app.log" >&2 || true
+  echo "--- update server log ---" >&2
+  cat "$WORK/server.log" >&2 || true
+  exit 1
+fi
+echo "OK: the running $OLD_VERSION replaced its own AppImage with $NEW_VERSION"
+
+kill "$APP_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
+wait "$APP_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
+APP_PID=""
+
+say "Running the updated app; it should see $NEW_VERSION and download nothing"
+: > "$WORK/server.log"
+(
+  cd "$WORK/run"
+  ./studio.AppImage > "$WORK/app-2.log" 2>&1
+) &
+APP_PID=$!
+sleep 15
+
+if ! grep -q "GET /latest.json" "$WORK/server.log"; then
+  echo "The updated app never checked the feed." >&2
+  cat "$WORK/server.log" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+if grep -q "GET /studio-$NEW_VERSION.AppImage" "$WORK/server.log"; then
+  echo "The updated app tried to download the release it is already running." >&2
+  cat "$WORK/server.log" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+echo "OK: the updated app reports no update and downloads nothing"
+
+say "Updater verified end to end"

 def _fenced_block_after(section: str, heading: str) -> list[str]:

+"""One canonical way to run the stack locally, everywhere it is documented.
+
+`python scripts/dev.py` starts the MCP server and the Studio sidecar together.
+Guides that walk a reader through running locally must use it, and no guide may
+quietly offer a second way (a bare uvicorn, the sidecar module, an old client).
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from pathlib import Path
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+CANONICAL = "python scripts/dev.py"
+
+# Guides that tell a reader how to run the project on their machine.
+LOCAL_GUIDES = (
+    ROOT / "README.md",
+    ROOT / "docs" / "living-studio.md",
+    ROOT / "docs" / "local-llm.md",
+    ROOT / "docs" / "deployment.md",
+)
+
+# Commands that would start the stack a different way. The MCP server alone is
+# a supported entry point (`python -m agentic_odi_mcp_server`) and is not listed.
+COMPETING_COMMANDS = (
+    "streamlit run",
+    "make dev",
+    "uvicorn ",
+    "python -m agentic_odi_studio_api",
+)
+
+
+def _docs() -> list[Path]:
+    return [ROOT / "README.md", *sorted((ROOT / "docs").glob("*.md"))]
+
+
+def test_every_local_guide_uses_the_canonical_command() -> None:
+    missing = [
+        str(guide.relative_to(ROOT))
+        for guide in LOCAL_GUIDES
+        if CANONICAL not in guide.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+    ]
+
+    assert not missing, f"These guides do not mention {CANONICAL!r}: {', '.join(missing)}"
+
+
+def test_no_guide_offers_a_competing_launch_command() -> None:
+    offenders: list[str] = []
+    for path in _docs():
+        text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+        for command in COMPETING_COMMANDS:
+            if command in text:
+                offenders.append(f"{path.relative_to(ROOT)}: {command.strip()}")
+
+    assert not offenders, "Competing launch commands: " + "; ".join(offenders)

+"""The README's Code Overview table must match the actual workspace.
+
+The table is hand-maintained, so it can quietly omit a new distribution or keep
+one that was deleted. This test reads the uv workspace and the distributions'
+own pyproject files, then checks the table in both directions.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import re
+from pathlib import Path
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+README = ROOT / "README.md"
+
+
+def _workspace_members() -> list[str]:
+    text = (ROOT / "pyproject.toml").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+    block = text.split("[tool.uv.workspace]", 1)[1]
+    members = block.split("members = [", 1)[1].split("]", 1)[0]
+    return re.findall(r'"([^"]+)"', members)
+
+
+def _distribution_name(member: str) -> str:
+    text = (ROOT / member / "pyproject.toml").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+    match = re.search(r'^name = "([^"]+)"', text, re.MULTILINE)
+    assert match is not None, f"{member}/pyproject.toml has no project name"
+    return match.group(1)
+
+
+def _table_rows() -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
+    """``(path, distribution)`` for every row in the Code Overview table."""
+    readme = README.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+    section = readme.split("## Code Overview", 1)[1].split("\n## ", 1)[0]
+    rows = re.findall(r"^\| \*\*`([^`]+)`\*\* \| ([^|]+) \|", section, re.MULTILINE)
+    return [(path, distribution.strip().strip("`")) for path, distribution in rows]
+
+
+def test_every_distribution_appears_in_the_readme() -> None:
+    listed = {distribution for _, distribution in _table_rows()}
+    missing = sorted(
+        name for name in map(_distribution_name, _workspace_members()) if name not in listed
+    )
+
+    assert not missing, f"README Code Overview is missing: {', '.join(missing)}"
+
+
+def test_every_workspace_package_has_a_table_row() -> None:
+    rows = {Path(path.rstrip("/")).name for path, _ in _table_rows()}
+
+    for member in _workspace_members():
+        assert Path(member).name in rows, f"README Code Overview has no row for {member}"
+
+
+def test_the_table_names_no_distribution_that_does_not_exist() -> None:
+    real = {_distribution_name(member) for member in _workspace_members()}
+    claimed = {
+        distribution for _, distribution in _table_rows() if distribution.startswith("agentic-odi")
+    }
+
+    assert claimed == real, f"README lists unknown distributions: {sorted(claimed - real)}"

+"""The site ships two themes: the reader's choice wins, the OS decides the rest."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import re
+
+import pytest
+from site_support import SITE, all_pages, read_page
+
+THEME_JS = SITE / "assets" / "theme.js"
+
+# Every colour the page paints with, by token name. A theme that forgets one
+# leaves that surface on the other theme's palette.
+COLOUR_TOKENS = {
+    "--bg",
+    "--bg-raised",
+    "--bg-sunken",
+    "--text",
+    "--muted",
+    "--faint",
+    "--accent",
+    "--accent-strong",
+    "--accent-ink",
+    "--green",
+    "--amber",
+    "--line",
+    "--line-strong",
+    "--surface",
+    "--surface-hover",
+    "--glass",
+    "--hairline",
+    "--shadow-deep",
+}
+
+
+def _block(css: str, selector: str) -> dict[str, str]:
+    match = re.search(re.escape(selector) + r"\s*\{([^}]*)\}", css, re.DOTALL)
+    assert match is not None, f"{selector} is missing from the tokens"
+    return dict(
+        (name.strip(), value.strip().rstrip(";").strip())
+        for name, value in (
+            line.split(":", 1) for line in match.group(1).splitlines() if ":" in line
+        )
+    )
+
+
+def _tokens() -> str:
+    return read_page("assets/tokens.css")
+
+
+def _all_names() -> set[str]:
+    return set(re.findall(r"^\s*(--[a-z-]+):", _tokens(), re.MULTILINE))
+
+
+def test_the_light_theme_overrides_every_colour_token():
+    dark = _block(_tokens(), ":root")
+    light = _block(_tokens(), ':root[data-theme="light"]')
+
+    missing = COLOUR_TOKENS - set(light)
+    assert not missing, f"the light theme leaves these on the dark palette: {sorted(missing)}"
+    # A light value for a token the dark theme never defines is a typo.
+    unknown = [name for name in light if name not in dark and name not in _all_names()]
+    assert not unknown, f"the light theme sets unknown tokens: {sorted(unknown)}"
+    assert dark["--bg"] != light["--bg"]
+
+
+def test_the_light_theme_is_actually_light():
+    light = _block(_tokens(), ':root[data-theme="light"]')
+
+    assert light["--bg"] == "#f7f8fb"
+    assert light["--text"] == "#12131a"
+    assert light["--bg"] != _block(_tokens(), ":root")["--bg"]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("page", all_pages())
+def test_every_page_offers_the_theme_toggle(page: str):
+    html = read_page(page)
+
+    assert 'class="theme-toggle"' in html
+    assert 'aria-label="Switch to the light theme"' in html
+    assert "theme-toggle__sun" in html and "theme-toggle__moon" in html
+
+
+def test_the_theme_is_chosen_before_the_stylesheets_render():
+    html = read_page("index.html")
+
+    script = html.index("assets/theme.js")
+    tokens = html.index("assets/tokens.css")
+    style = html.index("assets/style.css")
+
+    assert script < tokens < style
+
+
+def test_the_theme_script_defers_to_the_os_and_remembers_the_choice():
+    source = THEME_JS.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+
+    assert "(prefers-color-scheme: light)" in source
+    assert "agentic-odi.theme" in source
+    assert 'setAttribute("data-theme"' in source
+
+
+def test_the_toggle_updates_the_switch_in_both_themes():
+    source = (SITE / "assets" / "main.js").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+
+    assert "Switch to the dark theme" in source
+    assert "Switch to the light theme" in source
+    assert "localStorage.setItem(THEME_KEY" in source

> **TL;DR** — Six of the seven open pull requests on this repository contain a single commit that quietly replaces the whole tree with an old snapshot, deleting nine to eleven features that were already merged. They pass CI, because the reverted tree is internally consistent. Their descriptions are also materially false — one claims "20 touch-first improvements" and ships three CSS blocks and five tests; another claims to "delegate knowledge storage to external systems" and adds a URL field. After this issue, a pull request that deletes a file that exists on `main`, or whose description does not match its diff, fails CI before a human ever reads it.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Area** | `area/ci` |
| **Priority** | `priority/high` |
| **Kind** | specification |
| **Depends on** | — |
| **Related PRs** | #62, #63, #64, #65, #66, #70 |
| **Blocks** | #87 |

---

## The problem

**The pattern.** Every one of the six machine-generated branches (`google-labs-jules[bot]`) contains a *tree-replacement* commit — one commit touching 100+ files with roughly 20,000 deletions, dated 20:40–20:43, applied to branches whose real work was committed at 15:53–16:15.

| PR | Branch | Real work (first commit) | Tree-replacement commit | Net deletions |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #70 | `feat/signals-evidence-delegation-mvp-…` | `81f99a80` — 21 files, +1001/−26 | `c5198e55` — 107 files, +1326/−13524 | −11,849 |
| #66 | `feat/mobile-ux-elevation-…` | `d28d6a6e` — 7 files, +163/−7 | `fcccb4d0` — 158 files, +1981/−21830 | −21,715 |
| #65 | `feat/on-device-llm-fallback-router-…` | `3ff731b8` — 10 files, +382/−1 | `713a8cd2` — 161 files, +1758/−22013 | −21,825 |
| #64 | `feat/v2mom-context-capture-…` | `cf8e9489` — 11 files, +114/−5 | `76192e1b` — 108 files, +1327/−12939 | −12,926 |
| #63 | `jules-12210456461843385903-14563de9` | `3714baee` — 4 files, +7/−3 | `040a65a5` — 157 files, +1668/−21747 | −21,745 |
| #62 | `feat/cloud-agent-work-scheduling-…` | `f849c394` — 27 files, +1699/−5 | `75b60e08` — 105 files, +1332/−13594 | −12,924 |

**What those tree-replacement commits delete** — features that were already merged and shipped:

| Deleted file | Feature it carried | Merged in |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/flags.py`, `settings.py` | feature flags | #72 |
| `apps/studio-api/.../studio/changelog.py` | the changelog drawer | #60 |
| `apps/studio-api/.../studio/connectors.py` | MCP ↔ Studio connectors | #56 |
| `apps/studio-api/.../studio/ui_spec.py` | generative UI surfaces | #55 |
| `apps/studio/src/ui/catalog.ts`, `cards.tsx`, `protocol.ts` | the generative UI protocol | #55 |
| `apps/studio/src/onboarding/FirstRunWizard.tsx` | the first-run wizard | #69 |
| `apps/studio/src/components/notifications/CatchUpFeed.tsx` | catch-up notifications | #58 |
| `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/events.py`, `tests/test_events.py` | the event-sourced store | #42 |
| `apps/studio/src/components/setup/SetupConversation.tsx` | the context conversation | #43 |

Merging **any one** of the six would silently revert all of the above. `apps/studio/src/styles/theme.css` drops from 3,094 lines to 557–2,207 depending on the branch.

**Why CI did not catch it.** The six branches are internally consistent — the reverted tree compiles and its own tests pass. `ci.yml` has no job that looks at the *shape* of a diff. The only structural guard is the "Verify generated API types are up to date" step in the `studio` job, and it does not fire for deletions of files that are not API types.

**Why the descriptions did not catch it.** The PR bodies are machine-generated and materially false:

- #66 claims "20 touch-first micro-improvements" and "Vitest Unit Tests … 29 total tests passing" — the branch has **5** tests. It claims a mobile slide-over drawer built on `ChatCopilot.tsx`, a header switcher in `StudioHeader.tsx`, and swipeable tabs in `CanvasTabs.tsx` — **none of those three files exist on `main`**. It claims "All 546 pytest suite tests pass" while *deleting* seven test files.
- #65 claims an "on-device LLM fallback and multi-tier model router" — the "LLM" is a four-branch keyword matcher; `router.py:39-41` is `def is_available(self) -> bool: return True`; the diff adds **zero dependencies**; and `docs/local-llm.md` §6 promises a Settings UI and a config file for the routing mode, neither of which exists.
- #64 claims the assistant "continuously detects and refines V2MOM artifacts" — the entire change is **one line of prompt text**. There is no detection, extraction, or refinement code.
- #62 claims "cloud agent work scheduling" — `services.py:391` on that branch writes `"Executed mock cloud agent task '{work.name}' successfully"` and sets `status=COMPLETED`. No agent is dispatched. The CLI advertises ISO, relative and cron expressions; **none of the three is parsed**.
- #70 claims "delegation of full knowledge storage to external systems" — nothing delegates. The diff adds a `url: str | None` field.

**A human reviewing only the bodies would approve all six.**

**And the ruleset does not help.** The `main-requires-ci-green` ruleset has `bypass_actors: [{actor_id: 5, actor_type: RepositoryRole, bypass_mode: "always"}]` — the repository owner can merge to `main` with the check unsatisfied, with no warning. And `strict_required_status_checks_policy: false` means a branch that has never run CI can satisfy the check. #70 and #64 currently have **no `CI green` run on their head SHA**; they are blocked only because the owner has not used the bypass.

## What a person experiences

A pull request arrives. Before a human reads it, CI has already asked the two questions that matter: *"does this delete anything that is already shipped?"* and *"does the description match what the code does?"* A PR that reverts eleven merged features fails with a list of exactly which files it would remove and which release they shipped in. A PR that says it delivers twenty improvements and delivers three fails with a diff of the discrepancy. The reviewer reads a body they can trust, because a machine checked it.

## Specification

### 9.1 A diff-shape gate

Add `.github/workflows/pr-guardrails.yml`, triggered on `pull_request`. It must not need any secrets, and it must not be bypassable by a ruleset.

**Gate 1 — deletion budget.** A pull request must not delete a file that exists on the base branch, unless the deletion is explicitly allowed.

- Compute the set of files deleted relative to the base (`git diff --diff-filter=D --name-only origin/${{ github.base_ref }}...HEAD`).
- The gate **fails** if any deleted file is not in an allowlist.
- The allowlist is a YAML file at `.github/pr-guardrails/deletion-allowlist.yml`:
  ```yaml
  # One entry per approved deletion, with the reason and the issue that tracks it.
  - path: "apps/old/thing.tsx"
    issue: "<issue-number>"
    reason: "Replaced by apps/new/thing.tsx in <issue-number>"
  ```
- **Default deny.** An empty allowlist means no deletions are permitted.
- The message must list each deleted file and the release it shipped in, so the failure is actionable.

**Gate 2 — diff size.** A pull request must not exceed a deletion budget.

- `deletions > 500` in the total diff → fail, with a message asking the author to split the change.
- The threshold is configurable via `.github/pr-guardrails/config.yml` (`max_deletions`, `max_changed_files`).
- The check must **exclude** files that are legitimately regenerated (lockfiles, `openapi.json`, `schema.d.ts`, `coverage.xml`) via an explicit exclusion list — those are already generated and drifted by design.
- **The check must run on the cumulative PR diff, not per commit.** A tree-replacement commit buried in the middle of a branch is still visible in the cumulative diff. This is the whole point: all six broken PRs pass on a per-commit basis if you only look at the last commit.

**Gate 3 — branch freshness.** A pull request whose base is behind `origin/main` by more than N commits (default 50) must rebase. This does not catch the tree-replacement commit by itself, but it forces the rebase that would expose the conflict, and it is a cheap early signal. **This gate must be a warning, not a failure**, because rebases produce conflicts that a human resolves better.

### 9.2 A body-truth gate

A pull request description is a specification. It must match the diff.

- Extract the PR body (`github.event.pull_request.body`).
- **Rule 1 — file count.** If the body contains a claim of the form "N files" or "N+ files" (including a table of "micro-improvements" with N numbered rows), the gate counts the files actually changed and fails if the numbers differ by more than a small tolerance (default 20%). This catches #63 (claims 20 improvements, changes 4 files) and #66 (claims 20 improvements, changes 164 files but only 7 in the real commit).
- **Rule 2 — test-count claims.** If the body contains "N tests passing" or "N total tests", the gate counts the test functions added in the diff (`it(`, `test_`, `def test_`) and fails if the claim is off by more than 20%. This catches #66's "29 total tests" against 5.
- **Rule 3 — named-file claims.** If the body names a source file (a path with a recognizable extension), the gate asserts the file exists in the diff **or** exists on the base branch. This catches #66's claims about `ChatCopilot.tsx`, `StudioHeader.tsx`, and `CanvasTabs.tsx`, none of which exist.
- **Rule 4 — numbers in the title.** If the title contains "N " followed by a noun such as improvements, micro-improvements, features, or tests, the same file-count check applies.
- The gate emits a **warning comment** on the PR (not a failure) for rules 1–4, because natural language is hard to parse and a false positive is expensive. **The failure is reserved for the diff-shape gate**, which is deterministic.
- A companion script, `scripts/pr_guards.py`, holds the logic so it is unit-testable. Tests live in `tests/scripts/test_pr_guards.py`.

### 9.3 A fabrication guard on the code itself

A separate check, in the same workflow, greps the diff for patterns that have actually shipped in this repository's history:

- `mock` in a docstring or a comment **on a line that also returns a fabricated value** — for example `services.py:391`'s `"Executed mock cloud agent task"`.
- `is_available` implementations that `return True` unconditionally.
- Hardcoded numeric "result" strings that look like a measurement (`"3,000 hours of developer agony"`).
- A `TODO`, `FIXME`, `NotImplementedError`, or `pass  # stub` in a **new** line of the diff.

This check reports a **warning** with the file and line, and links to the issue that must resolve it. It does not block, because a legitimate word "mock" in a test file must not fail a build. Exclude `**/tests/**` and `**/test_*.py`.

### 9.4 The ruleset must be tightened

- The `main-requires-ci-green` ruleset must set `strict_required_status_checks_policy: true`, so a branch that has never run CI cannot satisfy the check.
- The admin bypass must be changed from `bypass_mode: "always"` to `bypass_mode: "pull_request"` (or removed). **A bypass that is always on is not a gate.**
- A **second required check** is added to the ruleset: `PR guardrails` (the workflow from 9.1). A PR that deletes shipped files must not be mergeable, even by an admin.
- **Note for the implementer:** ruleset changes are repository settings, not files. Do them with `gh api` / the API, and record the change in `docs/architecture/README.md` so it is not lost. `gh api repos/alehar9320/agentic-odi/rulesets` lists the current ruleset (`id 25356329`).

### 9.5 A merge template that asks the right questions

Update `.github/pull_request_template.md` to require:

- **What a person experiences** — the user-visible change, in user terms. Not a list of files.
- **How this was verified** — the exact commands that were run, and their output.
- **What this does NOT do** — the explicit scope boundary.
- **For machine-generated work:** a **Diff summary** line stating the true file count, the true test count, and the true net line delta, and a **Mock/stub disclosure** listing anything simulated.

A template that asks for the true numbers makes the body-truth gate's job easier and makes the human's job faster.

### 9.6 A machine-readable "what this PR really does" artifact

`.github/pull_request_template.md` gains a fenced block:

````markdown
```json
{"changed_files": 7, "tests_added": 5, "net_lines": 156, "simulated": [], "breaking": []}
```
````

The gate parses it, compares it against the actual diff, and fails on a mismatch of more than the tolerance. This is deterministic and becomes the primary signal; the natural-language rules in 9.2 are the fallback for PRs that omit the block.

## Non-negotiable constraints

| PR | Branch | Real work (first commit) | Tree-replacement commit | Net deletions |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #70 | `feat/signals-evidence-delegation-mvp-…` | `81f99a80` — 21 files, +1001/−26 | `c5198e55` — 107 files, +1326/−13524 | −11,849 |
| #66 | `feat/mobile-ux-elevation-…` | `d28d6a6e` — 7 files, +163/−7 | `fcccb4d0` — 158 files, +1981/−21830 | −21,715 |
| #65 | `feat/on-device-llm-fallback-router-…` | `3ff731b8` — 10 files, +382/−1 | `713a8cd2` — 161 files, +1758/−22013 | −21,825 |

| #63 | `jules-12210456461843385903-14563de9` | `3714baee` — 4 files, +7/−3 | `040a65a5` — 157 files, +1668/−21747 | −21,745 |
| #62 | `feat/cloud-agent-work-scheduling-…` | `f849c394` — 27 files, +1699/−5 | `75b60e08` — 105 files, +1332/−13594 | −12,924 |

| Deleted file | Feature it carried | Merged in |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/flags.py`, `settings.py` | feature flags | #72 |
| `apps/studio-api/.../studio/changelog.py` | the changelog drawer | #60 |
| `apps/studio-api/.../studio/connectors.py` | MCP ↔ Studio connectors | #56 |
| `apps/studio-api/.../studio/ui_spec.py` | generative UI surfaces | #55 |
| `apps/studio/src/ui/catalog.ts`, `cards.tsx`, `protocol.ts` | the generative UI protocol | #55 |
| `apps/studio/src/onboarding/FirstRunWizard.tsx` | the first-run wizard | #69 |
| `apps/studio/src/components/notifications/CatchUpFeed.tsx` | catch-up notifications | #58 |
| `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/events.py`, `tests/test_events.py` | the event-sourced store | #42 |
| `apps/studio/src/components/setup/SetupConversation.tsx` | the context conversation | #43 |

Merging **any one** of the six would silently revert all of the above. `apps/studio/src/styles/theme.css` drops from 3,094 lines to 557–2,207 depending on the branch.

**Why CI did not catch it.** The six branches are internally consistent — the reverted tree compiles and its own tests pass. `ci.yml` has no job that looks at the *shape* of a diff. The only structural guard is the "Verify generated API types are up to date" step in the `studio` job, and it does not fire for deletions of files that are not API types.

**Why the descriptions did not catch it.** The PR bodies are machine-generated and materially false:

- #66 claims "20 touch-first micro-improvements" and "Vitest Unit Tests … 29 total tests passing" — the branch has **5** tests. It claims a mobile slide-over drawer built on `ChatCopilot.tsx`, a header switcher in `StudioHeader.tsx`, and swipeable tabs in `CanvasTabs.tsx` — **none of those three files exist on `main`**. It claims "All 546 pytest suite tests pass" while *deleting* seven test files.
- #65 claims an "on-device LLM fallback and multi-tier model router" — the "LLM" is a four-branch keyword matcher; `router.py:39-41` is `def is_available(self) -> bool: return True`; the diff adds **zero dependencies**; and `docs/local-llm.md` §6 promises a Settings UI and a config file for the routing mode, neither of which exists.
- #64 claims the assistant "continuously detects and refines V2MOM artifacts" — the entire change is **one line of prompt text**. There is no detection, extraction, or refinement code.
- #62 claims "cloud agent work scheduling" — `services.py:391` on that branch writes `"Executed mock cloud agent task '{work.name}' successfully"` and sets `status=COMPLETED`. No agent is dispatched. The CLI advertises ISO, relative and cron expressions; **none of the three is parsed**.
- #70 claims "delegation of full knowledge storage to external systems" — nothing delegates. The diff adds a `url: str | None` field.

**A human reviewing only the bodies would approve all six.**

**And the ruleset does not help.** The `main-requires-ci-green` ruleset has `bypass_actors: [{actor_id: 5, actor_type: RepositoryRole, bypass_mode: "always"}]` — the repository owner can merge to `main` with the check unsatisfied, with no warning. A pull request arrives. Before a human reads it, CI has already asked the two questions that matter: *"does this delete anything that is already shipped?"* and *"does the description match what the code does?"* A PR that reverts eleven merged features fails with a list of exactly which files it would remove and which release they shipped in. ### 9.1 A diff-shape gate

- Compute the set of files deleted relative to the base (`git diff --diff-filter=D --name-only origin/${{ github.base_ref }}...HEAD`).

  ```yaml
  - path: "apps/old/thing.tsx"
    issue: "<issue-number>"
    reason: "Replaced by apps/new/thing.tsx in <issue-number>"
  ```
- **Default deny.** An empty allowlist means no deletions are permitted.

- `deletions > 500` in the total diff → fail, with a message asking the author to split the change.

A pull request description is a specification. It must match the diff.

<skill_content name="test-driven-development">
# Skill: test-driven-development

# Test-Driven Development (TDD)

## Overview

Write the test first. Watch it fail. Write minimal code to pass.

**Core principle:** If you didn't watch the test fail, you don't know if it tests the right thing.

**Violating the letter of the rules is violating the spirit of the rules.**

## When to Use

**Always:**
- New features
- Bug fixes
- Refactoring
- Behavior changes

**Exceptions (ask your human partner):**
- Throwaway prototypes
- Generated code
- Configuration files

Thinking "skip TDD just this once"? Stop. That's rationalization.

## The Iron Law

```
NO PRODUCTION CODE WITHOUT A FAILING TEST FIRST
```

Write code before the test? Delete it. Start over.

**No exceptions:**
- Don't keep it as "reference"
- Don't "adapt" it while writing tests
- Don't look at it
- Delete means delete

Implement fresh from tests. Period.

## Red-Green-Refactor

```dot
digraph tdd_cycle {
    rankdir=LR;
    red [label="RED\nWrite failing test", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ffcccc"];
    verify_red [label="Verify fails\ncorrectly", shape=diamond];
    green [label="GREEN\nMinimal code", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccffcc"];
    verify_green [label="Verify passes\nAll green", shape=diamond];
    refactor [label="REFACTOR\nClean up", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccccff"];
    next [label="Next", shape=ellipse];

    red -> verify_red;
    verify_red -> green [label="yes"];
    verify_red -> red [label="wrong\nfailure"];
    green -> verify_green;
    verify_green -> refactor [label="yes"];
    verify_green -> green [label="no"];
    refactor -> verify_green [label="stay\ngreen"];
    verify_green -> next;
    next -> red;
}
```

### RED - Write Failing Test

Write one minimal test showing what should happen.

<Good>
```typescript
test('retries failed operations 3 times', async () => {
  let attempts = 0;
  const operation = () => {
    attempts++;
    if (attempts < 3) throw new Error('fail');
    return 'success';
  };

  const result = await retryOperation(operation);

  expect(result).toBe('success');
  expect(attempts).toBe(3);
});
```
Clear name, tests real behavior, one thing
</Good>

<Bad>
```typescript
test('retry works', async () => {
  const mock = jest.fn()
    .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
    .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
    .mockResolvedValueOnce('success');
  await retryOperation(mock);
  expect(mock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3);
});
```
Vague name, tests mock not code
</Bad>

**Requirements:**
- One behavior
- Clear name
- Real code (no mocks unless unavoidable)

### Verify RED - Watch It Fail

**MANDATORY. Never skip.**

```bash
npm test path/to/test.test.ts
```

Confirm:
- Test fails (not errors)
- Failure message is expected
- Fails because feature missing (not typos)

**Test passes?** You're testing existing behavior. Fix test.

**Test errors?** Fix error, re-run until it fails correctly.

### GREEN - Minimal Code

Write simplest code to pass the test.

<Good>
```typescript
async function retryOperation<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
  for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
    try {
      return await fn();
    } catch (e) {
      if (i === 2) throw e;
    }
  }
  throw new Error('unreachable');
}
```
Just enough to pass
</Good>

<Bad>
```typescript
async function retryOperation<T>(
  fn: () => Promise<T>,
  options?: {
    maxRetries?: number;
    backoff?: 'linear' | 'exponential';
    onRetry?: (attempt: number) => void;
  }
): Promise<T> {
  // YAGNI
}
```
Over-engineered
</Bad>

Don't add features, refactor other code, or "improve" beyond the test.

### Verify GREEN - Watch It Pass

**MANDATORY.**

```bash
npm test path/to/test.test.ts
```

Confirm:
- Test passes
- Other tests still pass
- Output pristine (no errors, warnings)

**Test fails?** Fix code, not test.

**Other tests fail?** Fix now.

**"Other tests" means the project's suite, not just your file.** A
green run of the test you wrote is not a green suite. Before you call
the change done, run the project's test command (bare `pytest`,
`npm test`, `cargo test` — whatever the repo uses) even when your task
named only one test file. A scope statement in your task bounds the
deliverable, not your verification. Any failure that run shows —
including one you didn't cause — goes in your report by name; a red
test you watched scroll past and didn't mention is a report falsified
by omission.

### REFACTOR - Clean Up

After green only:
- Remove duplication
- Improve names
- Extract helpers

Keep tests green. Don't add behavior.

### Repeat

Next failing test for next feature.

## Good Tests

| Quality | Good | Bad |
|---------|------|-----|
| **Minimal** | One thing. "and" in name? Split it. | `test('validates email and domain and whitespace')` |
| **Clear** | Name describes behavior | `test('test1')` |
| **Shows intent** | Demonstrates desired API | Obscures what code should do |

When writing or changing any test, read [writing-good-tests.md](writing-good-tests.md) for the rules that keep tests honest:
- Name the production change that would make the test fail — before writing it
- Assert on real behavior, never on mock behavior
- Keep test-only code in test utilities, out of production classes
- Understand a dependency's side effects before mocking it

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Too simple to test" | Simple code breaks. Test takes 30 seconds. |
| "I'll test after" | Tests written after pass immediately — which proves nothing. They may test the wrong thing, test the implementation instead of the behavior, or miss the edge case you forgot. You never watched it fail, so you never proved it can catch the bug. Test-first forces that failure. |
| "Tests after achieve same goals (spirit not ritual)" | Tests-after answer "what does this do?"; tests-first answer "what should this do?" Tests written after are biased by the code you already wrote — you verify the cases you remembered, not the ones you'd have discovered. Coverage without proof the tests work. |
| "Already manually tested" | Manual testing is ad-hoc: no record of what you covered, no way to re-run it when the code changes, easy to forget cases under pressure. "Worked when I tried it" ≠ comprehensive. Automated tests run the same way every time. |
| "Deleting X hours is wasteful" | Sunk cost fallacy — that time is already spent either way. The real choice: rewrite with TDD (high confidence) vs. keep it and bolt tests on after (low confidence, likely bugs). Keeping code you can't trust is the waste. |
| "Keep as reference, write tests first" | You'll adapt it. That's testing after. Delete means delete. |
| "Need to explore first" | Fine. Throw away exploration, start with TDD. |
| "Test hard = design unclear" | Listen to test. Hard to test = hard to use. |
| "TDD will slow me down" | TDD IS the pragmatic path: catches bugs before commit, prevents regressions, lets you refactor without fear. "Pragmatic" shortcuts mean debugging in production — slower, not faster. |
| "Manual test faster" | Manual doesn't prove edge cases. You'll re-test every change. |
| "Existing code has no tests" | You're improving it. Add tests for existing code. |

## Red Flags - STOP and Start Over

- Code before test
- Test after implementation
- Test passes immediately
- Can't explain why test failed
- Tests added "later"
- Rationalizing "just this once"
- "I already manually tested it"
- "Tests after achieve the same purpose"
- "It's about spirit not ritual"
- "Keep as reference" or "adapt existing code"
- "Already spent X hours, deleting is wasteful"
- "TDD is dogmatic, I'm being pragmatic"
- "This is different because..."

**All of these mean: Delete code. Start over with TDD.**

## Example: Bug Fix

**Bug:** Empty email accepted

**RED**
```typescript
test('rejects empty email', async () => {
  const result = await submitForm({ email: '' });
  expect(result.error).toBe('Email required');
});
```

**Verify RED**
```bash
$ npm test
FAIL: expected 'Email required', got undefined
```

**GREEN**
```typescript
function submitForm(data: FormData) {
  if (!data.email?.trim()) {
    return { error: 'Email required' };
  }
  // ...
}
```

**Verify GREEN**
```bash
$ npm test
PASS
```

**REFACTOR**
Extract validation for multiple fields if needed.

## Verification Checklist

Before marking work complete:

- [ ] Every new function/method has a test
- [ ] Watched each test fail before implementing
- [ ] Each test failed for expected reason (feature missing, not typo)
- [ ] Wrote minimal code to pass each test
- [ ] All tests pass
- [ ] Output pristine (no errors, warnings)
- [ ] Tests use real code (mocks only if unavoidable)
- [ ] Edge cases and errors covered

Can't check all boxes? You skipped TDD. Start over.

## When Stuck

| Problem | Solution |
|---------|----------|
| Don't know how to test | Write wished-for API. Write assertion first. Ask your human partner. |
| Test too complicated | Design too complicated. Simplify interface. |
| Must mock everything | Code too coupled. Use dependency injection. |
| Test setup huge | Extract helpers. Still complex? Simplify design. |

## Debugging Integration

Bug found? Write failing test reproducing it. Follow TDD cycle. Test proves fix and prevents regression.

Never fix bugs without a test.

## Final Rule

```
Production code → test exists and failed first
Otherwise → not TDD
```

No exceptions without your human partner's permission.

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash

jobs:
  # A PR with no description gives a reviewer nothing to check the diff
  # against, so an empty body fails the build before any expensive job runs.
  pr-body:
    if: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    steps:
      - name: Require a non-empty pull request body
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: |
          body="$(gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "$REPO" --json body --jq '.body')"
          if [ -z "$(printf '%s' "$body" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
            echo "::error::The pull request body is empty. Summarize the change and how you verified it."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK: pull request body is present"

  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Run Ruff Lint (no auto-fix)
        run: uv run ruff check .

      - name: Verify Ruff Formatting (no auto-fix)
        run: uv run ruff format --check .

      - name: Verify the mascot assets match the generator
        run: uv run python brand/tools/render.py --check

  typecheck:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Run Mypy
        run: uv run mypy apps brand packages

      - name: Run Mypy (website)
        run: uv run --directory website mypy .

  security:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Run Bandit
        run: uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r apps packages

      - name: Run Bandit (website)
        run: uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r website/

  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        python-version: ["3.10", "3.11", "3.12"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}

      - name: Pytest
        run: |
          uv run pytest \
            --cov=agentic_odi_cli \
            --cov=agentic_odi_connectors \
            --cov=agentic_odi_core \
            --cov=agentic_odi_mcp_server \
            --cov=agentic_odi_studio_api \
            --cov-report=term-missing \
            --cov-report=xml:coverage.xml

      - name: Upload coverage report
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: coverage-${{ matrix.python-version }}
          path: coverage.xml
          if-no-files-found: error

      # One upload per run is enough; the 3.12 report is the canonical one.
      - name: Upload coverage to Codecov
        if: ${{ matrix.python-version == '3.12' }}

from __future__ import annotations

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]

WORKFLOW = ROOT / ".github" / "workflows" / "ci.yml"

REQUIRED_SECTIONS = ("## Summary", "## What changed", "## Verification", "## Related issue")


def test_the_template_asks_for_the_four_sections() -> None:
    template = TEMPLATE.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    for section in REQUIRED_SECTIONS:
        assert section in template, f"{section} is missing from the PR template"


def test_ci_runs_the_body_gate_only_for_pull_requests() -> None:
    workflow = WORKFLOW.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    assert "\n  pr-body:\n" in workflow
    assert "github.event_name == 'pull_request'" in workflow


def test_the_gate_reads_the_body_through_the_api_and_fails_when_empty() -> None:

  smoke:

    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: CLI reports a version
        run: |
          version="$(uv run python -m agentic_odi_cli --version)"
          [ -n "$version" ]

      - name: CLI exposes connectors commands
        run: |
          help="$(uv run python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors --help)"
          echo "$help" | grep -q list
          echo "$help" | grep -q ingest
          echo "OK: connectors help"

      - name: Installer installs from a simulated release
        run: bash scripts/tests/install_e2e.sh

      - name: MCP server boots and serves /mcp
        run: |
          uv run python -m agentic_odi_mcp_server > /tmp/mcp_server.log 2>&1 &
          SERVER_PID=$!
          probe() {
            curl -sfX POST http://localhost:8000/mcp \
              -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
              -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"initialize","id":1,"params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"ci","version":"1"}}}' \
              -o /dev/null
          }
          ok=0
          for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
            if probe; then ok=1; break; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          kill "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          wait "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "MCP server did not respond on :8000/mcp"
            cat /tmp/mcp_server.log
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK: MCP server responded with 200"

      - name: Living Studio sidecar serves the studio API
        run: |

          SIDECAR_PID=$!

"""Generate and publish end-user "Download & Run" instructions for a GitHub release.

Pure functions:
    build_instructions_section(tag, repo, artifacts, checksums_text) -> str
    apply_instructions(body, section) -> str

CLI (``main``): fetches the release body/assets via ``gh``, grabs
``checksums.txt`` via ``curl``, builds the instructions section, applies it
idempotently to the release body, and publishes with ``gh release edit``
(unless ``--dry-run``).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

DOWNLOAD_START = "<!-- AGENTIC_ODI_DOWNLOAD_START -->"
DOWNLOAD_END = "<!-- AGENTIC_ODI_DOWNLOAD_END -->"

GITHUB_RELEASES = "https://github.com"


def _archive_target(name: str) -> str:
    """Strip the ``odi_<version>_`` prefix and archive suffix to expose ``<os>_<arch>``."""
    stem = name
    for suffix in (".tar.gz", ".zip"):
        if stem.endswith(suffix):
            stem = stem[: -len(suffix)]
            break
    if stem.startswith("odi_"):
        stem = stem[len("odi_") :]
    parts = stem.split("_")
    if len(parts) >= 3:
        return "_".join(parts[1:])
    return stem


def _platform(target: str) -> str:
    mapping = {
        "linux_x86_64": "Linux (x86_64)",
        "linux_arm64": "Linux (ARM64)",
        "macos_x86_64": "macOS (Intel)",
        "macos_arm64": "macOS (Apple Silicon)",
        "windows_x86_64": "Windows (x86_64)",
    }
    return mapping.get(target, target.replace("_", " ").title())


def _hash_for(checksums_text: str, name: str) -> str | None:
    for line in checksums_text.splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if not line:
            continue
        hash_, sep, fname = line.partition("  ")
        if not sep:
            hash_, sep, fname = line.partition(" ")
        fname = fname.lstrip("*").strip()
        if fname == name:
            return hash_.strip()
    return None


def build_instructions_section(
    tag: str, repo: str, artifacts: list[dict], checksums_text: str
) -> str:
    version = tag.lstrip("v")
    dl_base = f"{GITHUB_RELEASES}/{repo}/releases/download/{tag}"

    release_artifacts = [
        a for a in artifacts if a["name"] not in ("checksums.txt", "install.sh", "install.ps1")
    ]

    lines: list[str] = []
    lines.append("## 📦 Download & Run")

parts.text:
There is already `tests/scripts/test_pr_body_gate.py` and a `pr-body` job. Good — I should keep those and add new stuff.

Now let me look at the rest of ci.yml (already read through ci-green). Existing workflow uses setup action. The new workflow `pr-guardrails.yml` must be self-contained with no secrets. It needs to compute cumulative diff vs base.

Design of `scripts/pr_guards.py`:

Pure functions that take inputs (lists of files, diff text, body, title), return findings. CLI modes:

- `diff-shape --base-ref origin/main --head-ref HEAD --config .github/pr-guardrails/config.yml --allowlist ...` → exit 1 on failures.
- `body-truth --body-file ... --title ... --changed-files N --tests-added N` → warnings
- `fabrication --diff-file ...` → warnings
- Or one `check` command that does all.

For testability and for CI, best: a single CLI with subcommands, and pure logic functions.

Let me define the data model:

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FileChange:
    status: str  # A, M, D, R...
    path: str
    old_path: str | None = None
```

But git diff --name-status can include renames. For deletion detection, `git diff --diff-filter=D --name-only base...HEAD`. Note: a tree-replacement commit deletes files, but over the cumulative diff base...HEAD, if the file was added in the branch and then deleted, it wouldn't appear as deletion vs base. However tree-replacement deletes files that exist on base → they appear as D in base...HEAD cumulative diff (three-dot diff). Good.

For diff size: `git diff --numstat base...HEAD` gives added/deleted per file; exclude generated files. Sum deletions. Also count changed files.

For "release it shipped in": need to find release tag containing the file. Simplest: `git tag --contains <commit-that-last-touched-file>`? Better: for each deleted file, find the commit on base that last modified it: `git log -1 --format=%H origin/$base -- path`, then find tags containing that commit `git tag --contains <sha> --sort=v:refname | head -1`. If none, "unreleased". That may be slow for many files but acceptable. Could implement via a function that takes a mapping or a callback. For unit tests, inject a `release_lookup: Callable[[str], str]`.

The spec says "The message must list each deleted file and the release it shipped in". So implement `resolve_release(path)` in CLI using git, with a fallback "unreleased". In tests, test formatting with injected lookup.

Config loading: `.github/pr-guardrails/config.yml` with max_deletions: 500, max_changed_files (default? spec says configurable; default maybe 2000), max_behind: 50, generated exclusions list, tolerances.

Allowlist YAML: list of {path, issue, reason}. Support globs? Spec says one entry per path; I'll support exact and fnmatch globs.

JSON block parsing: fenced ```json block in body with keys changed_files, tests_added, net_lines, simulated, breaking. Parse the first fenced json block. Compare: changed_files and tests_added within tolerance (20%), net_lines maybe absolute tolerance? Spec: "fails on a mismatch of more than the tolerance". Tolerance default 20%. net_lines could be within 20% too, but with small numbers 20% is harsh; use max(20%, absolute?) Hmm. Keep simple: relative tolerance on changed_files and tests_added; net_lines compare with tolerance of max(20%, 10 lines)? I'll implement `within_tolerance(claimed, actual, tolerance)` handling zero: if actual == 0 → claimed must be 0; else abs(claimed-actual)/actual <= tolerance. For net_lines, actual can be 0/negative. Use absolute difference <= max(10, abs(actual)*tolerance). Document.

Body truth rules:
- Rule 1 file count: regex for `(\d+)\+?\s+files` (case-insensitive). Also "table of micro-improvements with N numbered rows" — count numbered rows? Spec says if body contains a claim "N files", count. For the table, maybe detect numbered list rows count. I'll implement: collect claims of `(\d+)\s+(?:\+?\s+)?files` and numbered list items `^\s*\d+[.)]\s+` count when body mentions "improvement". """Unit tests for scripts/pr_guards.py (issue #86)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

from pr_guards import (
    GuardConfig,
    build_diff_args,
    changed_files_from_status,
    check_deletions,
    check_diff_budget,
    check_freshness,
    guard_diff_shape,
    is_generated,
    parse_name_status,
    parse_numstat,
)


def _release(path: str) -> str:
    return "v1.2.3"


# --- Gate 1: deletion budget -------------------------------------------------


def test_deleting_a_shipped_file_fails_and_names_the_release() -> None:
    errors = check_deletions(
        ["apps/old/thing.tsx"],
        allowlist=[],
        release_lookup=_release,
    )

    assert len(errors) == 1
    assert "apps/old/thing.tsx" in errors[0]
    assert "v1.2.3" in errors[0]


def test_an_empty_allowlist_denies_every_deletion() -> None:
    errors = check_deletions(
        ["a.py", "b.py"],
        allowlist=[],
        release_lookup=_release,
    )

    assert len(errors) == 2


def test_an_allowlisted_deletion_passes() -> None:
    allowlist = [{"path": "apps/old/thing.tsx", "issue": "123", "reason": "moved"}]

    errors = check_deletions(["apps/old/thing.tsx"], allowlist=allowlist, release_lookup=_release)

    assert errors == []


def test_the_allowlist_supports_globs() -> None:
    allowlist = [{"path": "apps/old/*.tsx", "issue": "123", "reason": "moved"}]

    errors = check_deletions(["apps/old/a.tsx", "apps/old/b.tsx"], allowlist, _release)

    assert errors == []


def test_missing_release_is_reported_as_unreleased() -> None:
    errors = check_deletions(["new.py"], allowlist=[], release_lookup=lambda _p: None)

    assert len(errors) == 1
    assert "unreleased" in errors[0]


# --- Gate 2: diff size -------------------------------------------------------


def test_exceeding_the_deletion_budget_fails() -> None:
    numstat = {"a.py": (0, 400), "b.py": (0, 200)}

    errors = check_diff_budget(numstat, GuardConfig(max_deletions=500))

    assert len(errors) == 1
    assert "600" in errors[0]


def test_staying_under_the_deletion_budget_passes() -> None:
    numstat = {"a.py": (10, 20)}

    assert check_diff_budget(numstat, GuardConfig(max_deletions=500)) == []


def test_generated_files_are_excluded_from_the_budget() -> None:
    numstat = {"uv.lock": (0, 5000), "package-lock.json": (0, 5000), "a.py": (1, 1)}

    assert check_diff_budget(numstat, GuardConfig(max_deletions=500)) == []


def test_generated_detection_covers_the_documented_paths() -> None:
    config = GuardConfig()

    for path in ("uv.lock", "apps/studio/src/api/schema.d.ts", "openapi.json", "coverage.xml"):
        assert is_generated(path, config), path
    assert not is_generated("apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/cli.py", config)


def test_exceeding_the_changed_file_budget_fails() -> None:
    numstat = {f"f{i}.py": (1, 0) for i in range(11)}

    errors = check_diff_budget(numstat, GuardConfig(max_changed_files=10))

    assert len(errors) == 1
    assert "11" in errors[0]


# --- Gate 3: branch freshness ------------------------------------------------


def test_a_stale_branch_is_a_warning_not_an_error() -> None:
    result = guard_diff_shape(
        deleted=[],
        numstat={},
        allowlist=[],
        config=GuardConfig(max_behind=50),
        release_lookup=_release,
        behind=51,
    )

    assert result.errors == []
    assert any("51" in warning for warning in result.warnings)


def test_a_fresh_branch_has_no_freshness_warning() -> None:
    result = guard_diff_shape(
        deleted=[],
        numstat={},
        allowlist=[],
        config=GuardConfig(max_behind=50),
        release_lookup=_release,
        behind=3,
    )

    assert result.warnings == []


def test_check_freshness_returns_the_warning() -> None:
    warnings = check_freshness(10, GuardConfig(max_behind=5))

    assert len(warnings) == 1


# --- Diff parsing and cumulative (three-dot) semantics ----------------------


def test_parse_name_status_handles_adds_modifies_and_deletes() -> None:
    status = "A\tnew.py\nM\told.py\nD\tgone.py\n"

    parsed = parse_name_status(status)

    assert parsed == [("A", "new.py", None), ("M", "old.py", None), ("D", "gone.py", None)]


def test_parse_name_status_handles_renames() -> None:
    parsed = parse_name_status("R100\told.py\tnew.py\n")

    assert parsed == [("R100", "new.py", "old.py")]


def test_parse_numstat_handles_binary_files() -> None:
    parsed = parse_numstat("10\t2\ta.py\n-\t-\tb.png\n")

    assert parsed == {"a.py": (10, 2), "b.png": (0, 0)}


def test_changed_files_from_status_counts_every_entry() -> None:
    parsed = parse_name_status("A\ta.py\nM\tb.py\nD\tc.py\n")

    assert changed_files_from_status(parsed) == 3


def test_diff_args_use_the_cumulative_three_dot_merge_base_diff() -> None:
    args = build_diff_args("origin/main", "HEAD")

    assert args == ["git", "diff", "--name-status", "origin/main...HEAD"]


def test_cumulative_diff_catches_a_mid_branch_tree_replacement(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    repo = tmp_path / "repo"
    repo.mkdir()

    def git(*args: str) -> None:
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", *args],
            cwd=repo,
            check=True,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
        )

    git("init", "-q", "-b", "main")
    git("config", "user.email", "test@example.com")
    git("config", "user.name", "Test")
    (repo / "shipped.py").write_text("shipped = True\n", encoding="utf-8")
    git("add", ".")
    git("commit", "-q", "-m", "base")

    git("checkout", "-q", "-b", "feature")
    (repo / "feature.py").write_text("feature = True\n", encoding="utf-8")
    git("add", ".")
    git("commit", "-q", "-m", "real work")

    (repo / "shipped.py").unlink()
    (repo / "feature.py").write_text("feature = False\n", encoding="utf-8")
    git("add", "-A")
    git("commit", "-q", "-m", "tree replacement")

    output = subprocess.run(
        build_diff_args("main", "HEAD"),
        cwd=repo,
        check=True,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
    ).stdout

    deleted = [new for status, new, _old in parse_name_status(output) if status == "D"]

    assert deleted == ["shipped.py"]

"""Deterministic pull-request guardrails (issue #86).

The logic lives here, not in YAML, so every rule is unit-tested. The GitHub
workflow in ``.github/workflows/pr-guardrails.yml`` only gathers the diff and
calls this module.

Three deterministic gates (failures):
  * deletion budget - a PR may not delete a shipped file unless allowlisted
  * diff size       - a PR may not delete more than ``max_deletions`` lines
  * JSON block      - the machine-readable diff summary must match the diff

Two advisory gates (warnings):
  * body truth      - natural-language claims about files and tests
  * fabrication     - patterns that have shipped fabricated work before
  * branch freshness - a stale base is worth a rebase, not a block

Everything is computed on the cumulative ``base...HEAD`` diff, never per
commit. A tree-replacement commit buried in the middle of a branch stays
visible in the cumulative diff.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import fnmatch
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Callable, Mapping, Sequence

# Files that are regenerated by design. Their churn is not a signal.
DEFAULT_GENERATED_EXCLUSIONS: tuple[str, ...] = (
    "uv.lock",
    "**/uv.lock",
    "package-lock.json",
    "**/package-lock.json",
    "yarn.lock",
    "**/yarn.lock",
    "pnpm-lock.yaml",
    "**/pnpm-lock.yaml",
    "Cargo.lock",
    "**/Cargo.lock",
    "poetry.lock",
    "**/poetry.lock",
    "*.lock",
    "**/openapi.json",
    "**/schema.d.ts",
    "**/coverage.xml",
)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class GuardConfig:
    """Tunable thresholds, read from ``.github/pr-guardrails/config.yml``."""

    max_deletions: int = 500
    max_changed_files: int = 2000
    max_behind: int = 50
    tolerance: float = 0.20
    generated_exclusions: tuple[str, ...] = DEFAULT_GENERATED_EXCLUSIONS


@dataclass
class GuardResult:
    """Errors fail the build; warnings annotate the PR."""

    errors: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    warnings: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)

    @property
    def failed(self) -> bool:
        return bool(self.errors)


ReleaseLookup = Callable[[str], str | None]


def build_diff_args(base_ref: str, head_ref: str) -> list[str]:
    """The cumulative diff. Three dots = merge-base diff, not last-commit."""
    return ["git", "diff", "--name-status", f"{base_ref}...{head_ref}"]


def parse_name_status(output: str) -> list[tuple[str, str, str | None]]:
    """Parse ``git diff --name-status`` into (status, path, old_path) tuples."""
    entries: list[tuple[str, str, str | None]] = []
    for line in output.splitlines():
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        parts = line.split("\t")
        status = parts[0]
        if status.startswith("R") or status.startswith("C"):
            entries.append((status, parts[2], parts[1]))
        else:
            entries.append((status, parts[1], None))
    return entries


def parse_numstat(output: str) -> dict[str, tuple[int, int]]:
    """Parse ``git diff --numstat``; binary files count as (0, 0)."""
    stats: dict[str, tuple[int, int]] = {}
    for line in output.splitlines():
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        added, deleted, path = line.split("\t", 2)
        stats[path] = (0 if added == "-" else int(added), 0 if deleted == "-" else int(deleted))
    return stats


def changed_files_from_status(entries: Sequence[tuple[str, str, str | None]]) -> int:
    return len(entries)


def is_generated(path: str, config: GuardConfig) -> bool:
    return any(fnmatch.fnmatch(path, pattern) for pattern in config.generated_exclusions)


def _allowed(path: str, allowlist: Sequence[Mapping[str, object]]) -> bool:
    for entry in allowlist:
        pattern = str(entry.get("path", ""))
        if pattern and fnmatch.fnmatch(path, pattern):
            return True
    return False


def check_deletions(
    deleted: Sequence[str],
    allowlist: Sequence[Mapping[str, object]],
    release_lookup: ReleaseLookup,
) -> list[str]:
    """Fail every deletion that is not explicitly allowlisted."""
    errors: list[str] = []
    for path in deleted:
        if _allowed(path, allowlist):
            continue
        release = release_lookup(path)
        where = f"shipped in {release}" if release else "unreleased"
        errors.append(
            f"Deleted file {path!r} ({where}). Deleting a file that exists on the base "
            "branch is not allowed. If this is intentional, add an entry to "
            ".github/pr-guardrails/deletion-allowlist.yml naming the issue and reason."
        )
    return errors


def check_diff_budget(numstat: Mapping[str, tuple[int, int]], config: GuardConfig) -> list[str]:
    """Fail when the diff deletes too many lines or touches too many files."""
    counted = {path: stat for path, stat in numstat.items() if not is_generated(path, config)}
    deletions = sum(deleted for _added, deleted in counted.values())
    changed = len(counted)

    errors: list[str] = []
    if deletions > config.max_deletions:
        errors.append(
            f"The diff deletes {deletions} lines, over the {config.max_deletions}-line budget. "
            "Split the change, or add a generated-file exclusion for files that are "
            "regenerated by design."
        )
    if changed > config.max_changed_files:
        errors.append(
            f"The diff changes {changed} files, over the {config.max_changed_files}-file budget. "
            "Split the change."
        )
    return errors


def check_freshness(behind: int, config: GuardConfig) -> list[str]:
    """A stale base is a warning: rebases are best resolved by a human."""
    if behind > config.max_behind:
        return [
            f"This branch is {behind} commits behind the base branch "
            f"(limit {config.max_behind}). Rebase so the diff is computed against "
            "the current base."
        ]
    return []


def guard_diff_shape(
    *,
    deleted: Sequence[str],
    numstat: Mapping[str, tuple[int, int]],
    allowlist: Sequence[Mapping[str, object]],
    config: GuardConfig,
    release_lookup: ReleaseLookup,
    behind: int = 0,
) -> GuardResult:
    errors = check_deletions(deleted, allowlist, release_lookup)
    errors.extend(check_diff_budget(numstat, config))
    return GuardResult(errors=errors, warnings=check_freshness(behind, config))


def load_config(path: Path) -> GuardConfig:
    """Read ``config.yml``; a missing file keeps the defaults."""
    if not path.exists():
        return GuardConfig()
    import yaml

    raw = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) or {}
    defaults = GuardConfig()
    return GuardConfig(
        max_deletions=int(raw.get("max_deletions", defaults.max_deletions)),
        max_changed_files=int(raw.get("max_changed_files", defaults.max_changed_files)),
        max_behind=int(raw.get("max_behind", defaults.max_behind)),
        tolerance=float(raw.get("tolerance", defaults.tolerance)),
        generated_exclusions=tuple(
            raw.get("generated_exclusions", defaults.generated_exclusions)
        ),
    )


def load_allowlist(path: Path) -> list[Mapping[str, object]]:
    """Read ``deletion-allowlist.yml``; a missing file denies every deletion."""
    if not path.exists():
        return []
    import yaml

    raw = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) or []
    if not isinstance(raw, list):
        raise ValueError(f"{path} must contain a list of deletion entries")
    return raw

```python
def _git(*args: str) -> str:
```
    import subprocess

    return subprocess.run(
        ["git", *args], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True
    ).stdout


def _release_lookup(base_ref: str) -> ReleaseLookup:
    cache: dict[str, str | None] = {}

    def lookup(path: str) -> str | None:
        if path in cache:
            return cache[path]
        release: str | None = None
        try:
            sha = _git("log", "-1", "--format=%H", base_ref, "--", path).strip()
            if sha:
                tags = _git("tag", "--contains", sha, "--sort=v:refname").splitlines()
                release = tags[0] if tags else None
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - an unknown release is "unreleased"
            release = None
        cache[path] = release
        return release

    return lookup


def _collect(base_ref: str) -> tuple[
    list[tuple[str, str, str | None]], dict[str, tuple[int, int]], str
]:
    status = parse_name_status(_git(*build_diff_args(base_ref, "HEAD")))
    numstat = parse_numstat(_git("diff", "--numstat", f"{base_ref}...HEAD"))
    diff = _git("diff", "--unified=0", f"{base_ref}...HEAD")
    return status, numstat, diff


def _emit(kind: str, message: str) -> None:

def _write_warnings(path: str | None, warnings: Sequence[str]) -> None:

name: PR guardrails

# Deterministic gates that a pull request cannot lie about its shape.
# No repository secrets: the gates only need the checked-out repository.
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, edited]

concurrency:
  group: pr-guardrails-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write

defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash

jobs:
  pr-guardrails:
    name: PR guardrails
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      # Full history so the cumulative base...HEAD diff and release tags exist.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Fetch the base branch
        run: |
          git fetch --no-tags origin \
            "${{ github.base_ref }}:refs/remotes/origin/${{ github.base_ref }}"

      # The diff-shape gate is the only gate that blocks, and it runs on the
      # cumulative diff: a tree-replacement commit in the middle of a branch
      # stays visible here.
      - name: Diff-shape gate
        if: always()
        run: |
          uv run python scripts/pr_guards.py diff-shape \
            --base-ref "origin/${{ github.base_ref }}"

      - name: Body-truth gate
        if: always()
        env:
          PR_BODY: ${{ github.event.pull_request.body }}
          PR_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
        run: |
          printf '%s' "$PR_BODY" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/pr-body.md"
          uv run python scripts/pr_guards.py body-truth \
            --base-ref "origin/${{ github.base_ref }}" \
            --body-file "$RUNNER_TEMP/pr-body.md" \
            --title "$PR_TITLE" \
            --warnings-out "$RUNNER_TEMP/body-warnings.txt"

      - name: Fabrication guard
        if: always()
        run: |
          uv run python scripts/pr_guards.py fabrication \
            --base-ref "origin/${{ github.base_ref }}" \
            --warnings-out "$RUNNER_TEMP/fabrication-warnings.txt"

      - name: Publish guardrail warnings
        if: always()
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: |
          message="$RUNNER_TEMP/guardrail-warnings.md"
          : > "$message"
          for file in "$RUNNER_TEMP/body-warnings.txt" "$RUNNER_TEMP/fabrication-warnings.txt"; do
            if [ -s "$file" ]; then
              {
                echo "## PR guardrails — warnings"
                echo
                echo '```'
                cat "$file"
                echo '```'
              } >> "$message"
            fi
          done
          if [ -s "$message" ]; then
            gh pr comment "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "$REPO" --body-file "$message" \
              --edit-last --create-if-none ||
              echo "note: could not post the warning comment (fork or token permissions)"
          fi

1:# Repository Architecture
5:## Layout
23:## Dependency Direction
44:## Persistence
55:## MCP Contract
59:## Entry Points
68:## Related
---
- `packages/core` depends on no other workspace package.
- `packages/connectors` depends on `core` only where it needs shared models.
- Every runnable app may depend on `core`; none of them imports another app.
- The React SPA only talks to `apps/studio-api` over `/api`; it never calls MCP or the LLM directly.
- The SPA's conversation runtime is assistant-ui, bound to the Studio's own
  store in `apps/studio/src/assistant/`. That directory
  is the whole bridge: `convert.ts` maps the two message models in both
  directions, `StudioRuntime.tsx` wires the runtime callbacks, and
  `attachments.ts` extracts files in the browser. The library is presentation
  only — it holds no product state and makes no network calls of its own.

## Persistence

- `SQLiteRepository` is the production default for the CLI, MCP server, and Studio API.
- The default database is `~/.agentic-odi/odi.db`, overridable with `AGENTIC_ODI_DB`.
- Studio conversation history and PM memory use a separate SQLite database,
  `~/.agentic-odi/studio.db`, overridable with `AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DB`. They are
  sidecar-local and never enter the ODI repository or the MCP contract.
- `build_repository()` chooses SQLite by default and `InMemoryRepository` when `AGENTIC_ODI_DB=:memory:`, which is what tests use.
- The CLI selects its backend with `--backend local|mcp` or `AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND`.
- The Studio API selects `local` (direct service calls) or `mcp` (passthrough) with `AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND` or `create_app(backend=...)`.

## MCP Contract

`packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/contract.py` owns `ToolName`, `ToolSpec`, `TOOL_SPECS`, and `TOOL_NAMES`. The live FastMCP registry is asserted against it by `tests/contract/test_mcp_contract.py`; the CLI's local handlers are checked by `tests/contract/test_cli_contract.py`.

## Entry Points

| Command | Module |
|---|---|
| `agentic-odi` | `agentic_odi_cli.cli:app` |
| `agentic-odi-server` / `agentic-odi-mcp-server` | `agentic_odi_mcp_server.mcp_server:main` |
| `agentic-odi-studio-api` | `agentic_odi_studio_api.main:main` |
| `uv run python scripts/dev.py` | Dev launcher (MCP + Studio API) |

## Related

- [Data flow](data-flow.md)
- [Testing](testing.md)
- [Decisions (ADRs)](adr/README.md) — why the architecture looks the way it does

## Pull Request Guardrails

`.github/workflows/pr-guardrails.yml` runs three gates on the cumulative
`base...HEAD` diff, so a tree-replacement commit buried in the middle of a
branch is still visible:

- **diff-shape** (blocking): refuses to delete a file that exists on the base
  branch unless it is listed in `.github/pr-guardrails/deletion-allowlist.yml`;
  refuses a diff that deletes more than `max_deletions` lines or changes more
  than `max_changed_files` files, excluding regenerated files. Thresholds live
  in `.github/pr-guardrails/config.yml`.
- **body-truth** (warns; the fenced JSON diff summary blocks): compares
  natural-language file/test claims and the machine-readable block against the
  real diff.
- **fabrication** (warns): flags new `TODO`/`FIXME`/`NotImplementedError`/stubs,
  unconditional `is_available`, hardcoded measurements, and "mock" returns.

The logic lives in `scripts/pr_guards.py`; the YAML only gathers the diff.
Unit tests are in `tests/scripts/test_pr_guards.py`.

## Summary

A pull request must not be able to lie about its shape or its description. This adds deterministic guardrails that run before a human reads the diff, so a branch that silently deletes shipped files, or a body that claims work it did not do, fails or is annotated by CI.

## What a person experiences

Before reviewing, CI answers two questions: *does this delete anything that is already shipped?* and *does the description match the diff?* A PR that deletes a base-branch file fails with the file name and the release it shipped in. A body whose file/test claims, named files, or JSON summary disagree with the diff gets a warning comment (the JSON block fails).

## What changed

- `scripts/pr_guards.py` — all gate logic, so it is unit-testable:
  - diff-shape: default-deny deletion allowlist, deletion/file budgets with generated-file exclusions, branch-freshness warning, all on the cumulative `base...HEAD` diff;
  - body-truth: file-count, test-count, named-file, and title-number rules (warnings), plus the fenced JSON diff summary (fails on mismatch);
  - fabrication: new TODO/FIXME/NotImplementedError/stub, unconditional `is_available`, hardcoded measurements, and `mock` returns (warnings, tests excluded).
- `.github/workflows/pr-guardrails.yml` — runs on `pull_request`, full history, fetches the base, needs no repository secrets.
- `.github/pr-guardrails/config.yml` and `deletion-allowlist.yml` — thresholds and an empty (deny-all) allowlist.
- `.github/pull_request_template.md` — experience, verification, scope, diff summary, mock/stub disclosure, and the JSON block.
- `docs/architecture/README.md` — records the ruleset change.
- `tests/scripts/test_pr_guards.py` — one test per rule, including a real git repository proving the cumulative diff catches a mid-branch tree-replacement commit.

## How this was verified

```

  1219 passed, 2 warnings

uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check .
  All checks passed! / 293 files already formatted

uv run mypy apps brand packages
  Success: no issues found in 162 source files

  ::error::Deleted file 'shipped.py' (shipped in v1.0.0)...

# body claim 7 files / JSON 7 when the diff has 2
uv run python scripts/pr_guards.py body-truth --base-ref main ...
  ::warning::... claims 7 files, but the diff changes 2
  ::error::The JSON diff summary claims changed_files=7, but the diff has 2
  pr-guardrails: 2 body-truth error(s)   # exit 1
```

## What this does NOT do

- Does not review code quality, and never approves a PR.
- Does not land the six tree-replacement branches' real work (#87).
- Does not make natural-language rules fail; only the deletion/budget rules and the JSON block mismatch fail.
